purpose: Human-review preparation for the existing IMAGE_NEEDED backlog; this file does not authorize generation or linking.

methodology.priority_1: Complex architecture, multi-stage process, structural/spatial concept, or reusable systems concept that prose alone communicates poorly.
methodology.priority_2: Useful comparison, process, metric, or conceptual aid; prose remains sufficient.
methodology.priority_3: Mostly illustrative, summary-oriented, UI-specific, or low incremental educational value.
methodology.quality_checks: Every request is checked for a title, a concrete draw/show instruction, a learner-notice statement, exact duplication, and time-sensitive UI wording.

requests.lesson_title: Introducing Deep Learning and the PyTorch Library
requests.title: Feature engineering versus representation learning
requests.show: A two-part diagram comparing a traditional ML pipeline where a practitioner manually creates features before a learning algorithm with a deep-learning pipeline where raw data enters a neural network that learns hierarchical features automatically during training
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that deep learning reduces manual feature design but typically increases dependence on data, training, and computation

requests.lesson_title: Introducing Deep Learning and the PyTorch Library
requests.title: High-level PyTorch project workflow
requests.show: A left-to-right pipeline showing raw data or storage, Dataset conversion to tensors, DataLoader batching, an untrained model, the training loop with loss and optimizer, a trained model, and deployment; include optional multi-GPU or multi-machine training beneath the training stage
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that the neural network is only one component in a complete deep learning system

requests.lesson_title: Pretrained Networks: From Image Recognition to Multimodal Models
requests.title: Pretrained image-classification inference pipeline
requests.show: A diagram showing an input photograph being resized/cropped/normalized into a tensor, passed through a pretrained classifier, producing one score for each ImageNet class, followed by top-k label selection
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that inference requires both the trained network and the correct input/output processing around it

requests.lesson_title: Pretrained Networks: From Image Recognition to Multimodal Models
requests.title: Neural-network architecture and forward pass
requests.show: A simplified left-to-right model diagram inspired by an image classifier, showing an input image passing through several learned processing blocks into a final vector of class scores; optionally annotate intermediate representations without reproducing source artwork
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that the input is progressively transformed and that the learned weights inside the blocks determine the transformations

requests.lesson_title: Pretrained Networks: From Image Recognition to Multimodal Models
requests.title: Inputs to diffusion inpainting
requests.show: A conceptual three-input diagram showing a text prompt, an original image, and a black/white edit mask entering an inpainting pipeline and producing an edited image
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that the prompt controls what to generate, the image defines the starting scene, and the mask constrains where changes may occur

requests.lesson_title: Pretrained Networks: From Image Recognition to Multimodal Models
requests.title: Iterative diffusion inpainting process
requests.show: A sequence of 4–6 stages showing the masked region beginning noisy and becoming gradually more structured while the unmasked background remains fixed, ending with a coherent localized edit
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that generation happens through repeated refinement rather than a single deterministic drawing step

requests.lesson_title: Pretrained Networks: From Image Recognition to Multimodal Models
requests.title: BLIP image-captioning mental model
requests.show: A conceptual pipeline showing an input image entering an image encoder, producing an embedding or visual representation, then entering a text decoder that generates a natural-language caption
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that the model bridges two modalities by turning visual information into a representation that can condition language generation

requests.title: Input-to-intermediate-to-output representations
requests.show: A simple neural-network pipeline showing a human-interpretable input on the left, several layers of floating-point intermediate representations in the middle, and a human-usable output on the right
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that the network repeatedly transforms numeric representations and that the hidden intermediate representations are task-dependent

requests.title: Scalar, vector, matrix, and 3D tensor
requests.show: A progression showing a single scalar, a one-dimensional vector, a two-dimensional matrix, and a three-dimensional stack with shape labels
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that tensors generalize familiar scalar/vector/matrix structures to arbitrary numbers of dimensions

requests.title: Broadcasting shape alignment
requests.show: A visual example showing a (1, 3) row tensor and a (3, 1) column tensor expanding conceptually to form a (3, 3) result, with dimensions aligned from the right
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that a dimension of size 1 can be virtually expanded and that broadcasting does not require manually duplicating values

requests.title: Python objects versus tensor storage
requests.show: A side-by-side diagram showing a Python list as references to individually boxed numeric objects and a tensor as a compact homogeneous contiguous block of unboxed numeric values
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice why tensors are more memory- and computation-friendly for large numerical collections

requests.title: Tensor storage with size, offset, and stride
requests.show: A one-dimensional storage block with indices, plus two tensor views laid over it; annotate one view with shape, storage offset, and per-dimension strides
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that tensor indexing is translated into positions in shared storage using metadata

requests.title: Transpose without copying
requests.show: A diagram showing one shared storage block referenced by an original 3x2 tensor and a transposed 2x3 tensor, with different stride arrows for each
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that the apparent matrix layout can change while the underlying storage remains the same

requests.title: CPU-to-GPU tensor workflow
requests.show: A diagram showing a tensor copied from CPU RAM to GPU memory, several operations occurring on the GPU while the data remains there, and an explicit transfer back to CPU at the end
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that device transfer and device computation are separate actions

requests.title: RGB image channels
requests.show: A color image shown alongside separate red, green, and blue intensity maps
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that a color image is represented as multiple aligned numerical channels rather than one scalar per pixel

requests.title: Image layout conversion
requests.show: A diagram showing an image tensor changing from H×W×C to C×H×W, with the same underlying pixel data but reordered logical axes
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that the meaning/order of dimensions changes even though the image content does not

requests.title: CT volume built from slices
requests.show: A stack of 2D grayscale scan slices arranged along a depth axis to form a 3D volume
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that depth is a spatial dimension, unlike RGB channels which represent different measured features at the same pixel location

requests.title: Choosing a representation for column types
requests.show: A simple flowchart distinguishing continuous, ordinal, and categorical variables and showing common representation choices such as normalized numeric values, ordered numeric or categorical treatment, and one-hot/embedding representation
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that representation should preserve the real meaning of the variable rather than blindly treating every number as continuous

requests.title: Flat time-series table to daily tensor
requests.show: A 2D table of hourly rows being grouped into blocks of 24 and transformed into a 3D tensor with separate day, variable, and hour axes
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that adding a time-period axis makes sequential structure explicit rather than treating every hour independently

requests.title: N×C×L versus N×L×C sequence layouts
requests.show: Two simplified 3D tensor diagrams comparing sample×variables×time with sample×time×variables
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that both can contain the same values, but axis ordering determines how conveniently the model and code access complete variable sequences

requests.title: Character, word, and embedding text representations
requests.show: A comparison showing character-level one-hot rows, word-level one-hot rows with a much larger vocabulary dimension, and a compact dense embedding vector for each word
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice the trade-off between sequence granularity, vocabulary size, and representation compactness

requests.title: Semantic embedding space
requests.show: A simple 2D conceptual embedding plot with related words clustered near one another and unrelated groups separated, making clear that real embeddings usually have many more dimensions
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that distance and direction in an embedding can encode relationships that one-hot vectors do not express

requests.title: Mental model of learning
requests.show: A loop diagram showing input and target entering a model, model output compared with target through a loss function, gradients flowing backward to parameters, and parameters being updated before the next forward pass
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that learning is an iterative feedback process driven by prediction error

requests.title: Noisy thermometer measurements
requests.show: A scatter plot with unknown thermometer reading on the horizontal axis and Celsius temperature on the vertical axis, showing an approximately linear trend with some noise
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that a straight line appears to be a reasonable first model even though the points are not perfectly aligned

requests.title: Absolute error versus squared error
requests.show: Two simple loss curves centered at zero error: a V-shaped absolute-error curve and a smooth U-shaped squared-error curve
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that both are minimized at zero but squared error is smooth and grows more strongly for large errors

requests.title: Gradient descent as parameter knobs
requests.show: A conceptual machine with two knobs labeled w and b and a loss display, with arrows showing adjustments toward lower loss
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that each parameter is adjusted according to how changing it affects the loss

requests.title: Numerical versus analytical gradient
requests.show: A curve with one slope estimated from two nearby points and another tangent slope drawn exactly at a point
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that finite differences approximate local change whereas differentiation gives the local derivative directly

requests.title: Converging versus diverging gradient descent
requests.show: Two bowl-shaped loss plots: one with steps jumping back and forth farther away from the minimum, and another with smaller steps approaching the minimum
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that the learning rate controls update size and can determine whether optimization converges or diverges

requests.title: Autograd forward and backward computation graph
requests.show: A small graph showing parameters feeding a linear model, prediction feeding a loss node, then backward arrows from loss through the model to parameter gradients
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that the forward pass records dependencies and backward traverses them in reverse to apply the chain rule

requests.title: Training and validation split
requests.show: A dataset divided into a larger training subset and a held-out validation subset, with parameter updates driven only by training data and validation data flowing only to an evaluation loss
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that validation observations are deliberately kept out of gradient-based fitting

requests.title: Training and validation loss scenarios
requests.show: Four small plots showing: neither loss decreasing; training decreasing while validation worsens; both decreasing together; and both decreasing with a stable gap
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should identify no learning, overfitting, ideal generalization trend, and acceptable generalization with different absolute losses

requests.lesson_title: Using a Neural Network to Fit the Data
requests.title: Same training loop, different model
requests.show: A diagram showing input and target entering the familiar training loop, with the model box changing from a linear equation to a neural network while loss, backward pass, optimizer, and validation stay the same
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that the model architecture changes but the training mechanics remain

requests.lesson_title: Using a Neural Network to Fit the Data
requests.title: Anatomy of an artificial neuron
requests.show: Input x enters a multiply-by-weight step, bias b is added, and the result passes through activation f to produce output
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice the linear transformation followed by a fixed nonlinear function

requests.lesson_title: Using a Neural Network to Fit the Data
requests.title: Simple multilayer neural network
requests.show: Input vector, two hidden layers, and an output layer connected left to right
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that intermediate representations are passed layer to layer

requests.lesson_title: Using a Neural Network to Fit the Data
requests.title: Tanh sensitive and saturated regions
requests.show: A tanh curve with the center marked as sensitive and the flat tails marked as saturated
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that changes near zero affect output more strongly than changes in the tails

requests.lesson_title: Using a Neural Network to Fit the Data
requests.title: Activation function comparison
requests.show: A grid of Tanh, Sigmoid, ReLU, LeakyReLU, and Hardtanh curves on common axes
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice differences in range, slope, and saturated/flat regions

requests.lesson_title: Using a Neural Network to Fit the Data
requests.title: Combining nonlinear neurons
requests.show: Several shifted and scaled activation curves shown individually and then combined into a more complicated nonlinear curve
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that simple units can compose into functions much richer than any one unit

requests.lesson_title: Using a Neural Network to Fit the Data
requests.title: Batched neural-network inputs and outputs
requests.show: Several samples enter the same model in parallel, labeled B×N_in, with B×N_out at the output
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that dimension 0 carries independent samples through the same learned function

requests.lesson_title: Using a Neural Network to Fit the Data
requests.title: Linear-Tanh-Linear neural network
requests.show: Two depictions of the same network: a node-and-arrow view and a block view labeled Linear(1,13), Tanh, Linear(13,1)
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that both diagrams represent the same computation at different abstraction levels

requests.lesson_title: Using a Neural Network to Fit the Data
requests.title: Linear fit versus neural-network fit
requests.show: Thermometer scatter points with a straight linear fit and a slightly curved neural-network fit following some noisy samples
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that greater capacity can fit noise even when the true process is simple

requests.lesson_title: Telling Birds from Airplanes: Learning from Images
requests.title: End-to-end bird-vs-airplane classifier
requests.show: A pipeline showing CIFAR-10 images entering preprocessing, a neural-network classifier, class scores, loss during training, and predicted bird/airplane labels during inference
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that the image classification system contains data preparation, model, loss, optimization, and evaluation

requests.lesson_title: Telling Birds from Airplanes: Learning from Images
requests.title: CIFAR-10 class samples
requests.show: A small grid with one or more example 32×32 RGB images from each of the ten CIFAR-10 classes
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice the tiny image size, the visual ambiguity, and that each sample belongs to one discrete class

requests.lesson_title: Telling Birds from Airplanes: Learning from Images
requests.title: PyTorch Dataset interface
requests.show: A dataset box exposing __len__ and __getitem__, with __getitem__(i) returning an image and an integer label
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that a Dataset provides an access interface and does not necessarily need to hold every transformed sample permanently in memory

requests.lesson_title: Telling Birds from Airplanes: Learning from Images
requests.title: CIFAR image before and after normalization
requests.show: The same image shown conceptually before normalization and after channel standardization, with a note that the normalized tensor can contain values outside 0..1 even though no information was intentionally removed
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that normalized data may look visually strange while still being useful to the model

requests.lesson_title: Telling Birds from Airplanes: Learning from Images
requests.title: Flattening an image into a feature vector
requests.show: A 3×32×32 RGB image tensor being reshaped into one long 3072-element vector before entering a fully connected neural network
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that flattening preserves numerical values but removes the explicit 2D spatial layout

requests.lesson_title: Telling Birds from Airplanes: Learning from Images
requests.title: Logits to probabilities with softmax
requests.show: A vector of raw class scores entering softmax and producing nonnegative probabilities that sum to 1, with the highest logit remaining the highest probability
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that softmax changes scale but preserves ranking

requests.lesson_title: Telling Birds from Airplanes: Learning from Images
requests.title: Negative log-likelihood curve
requests.show: A curve of -log(p) for correct-class probability p from near 0 to 1
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that assigning very small probability to the true class receives a very large penalty while loss approaches zero as p approaches 1

requests.lesson_title: Telling Birds from Airplanes: Learning from Images
requests.title: Full batch vs sample-wise vs minibatch optimization
requests.show: Three diagrams showing one update after all samples, one update after each individual sample, and one update after each small batch
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice the trade-off between gradient stability and update frequency

requests.lesson_title: Telling Birds from Airplanes: Learning from Images
requests.title: Dataset and DataLoader relationship
requests.show: A Dataset exposing indexed samples, a shuffled index order, and a DataLoader grouping those indices into minibatches before yielding image/label tensors
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that Dataset defines access to individual items while DataLoader controls batching and sampling order

requests.lesson_title: Telling Birds from Airplanes: Learning from Images
requests.title: Parameter explosion in a fully connected image layer
requests.show: A flattened 3072-value image fully connected to 1024 hidden units, with an annotation showing a 1024×3072 weight matrix and over 3 million parameters
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that every hidden unit needs a separate connection to every input pixel

requests.lesson_title: Telling Birds from Airplanes: Learning from Images
requests.title: Fully connected treatment of an image
requests.show: A 2D image flattened into a long vector with dense connections from every pixel value to every hidden unit
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that the network uses many connections but has no built-in notion of local neighborhoods

requests.lesson_title: Telling Birds from Airplanes: Learning from Images
requests.title: Same airplane shifted to a new image position
requests.show: Two small images containing the same airplane-like pattern at different coordinates, plus a flattened-vector view showing that different feature positions become active
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice why a fully connected classifier must relearn similar patterns at different locations

requests.title: Fully connected image processing versus convolution
requests.show: Left side shows a flattened image densely connected to hidden units; right side shows a small kernel applied locally at many positions
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that convolution reuses the same small set of weights instead of learning independent weights for every pixel-location relationship

requests.title: Sliding 3x3 convolution kernel
requests.show: A small 3×3 kernel overlaying one neighborhood of an image, with corresponding cells multiplied and summed to produce one output pixel, then the kernel shown sliding to the next position
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that the identical kernel weights are reused at every location

requests.title: Conv2d channel transformation
requests.show: Three RGB input channels feeding several 3×3 kernels and producing 16 output feature maps
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that one output channel combines information from all input channels using its own learned kernel bank

requests.title: Zero padding around a 2D input
requests.show: A small image grid surrounded by one border of zero-valued ghost pixels, with a 3×3 kernel centered over an original corner pixel
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that padding lets the kernel produce outputs at boundary locations

requests.title: Blur kernel and vertical-edge kernel effects
requests.show: Show the same simple image passed through a local averaging kernel and a vertical-edge detector, alongside the two 3×3 kernels
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that different local weight patterns emphasize different visual features

requests.title: Max pooling over 2x2 regions
requests.show: A small activation map divided into non-overlapping 2×2 cells, with the maximum value from each cell copied into a smaller output map
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that strong feature responses survive while spatial resolution is halved

requests.title: Receptive field growing with depth
requests.show: A sequence Conv3x3 -> MaxPool2x2 -> Conv3x3 with arrows tracing one deep output value back to a much larger area of the original image
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that small kernels can indirectly see large input regions when layers are stacked

requests.title: Complete baseline CNN with tensor shapes
requests.show: A block diagram of two convolution/activation/pooling stages followed by flatten and two fully connected layers, annotated with the tensor shape after each stage
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should practice tracing channels and spatial dimensions

requests.title: CPU DataLoader to GPU model pipeline
requests.show: DataLoader yields CPU minibatches, image and label tensors are transferred to GPU memory, the CNN runs on GPU, then scalar logging values return to Python
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that model parameters and input tensors must be on the same device

requests.title: Dropout during training versus evaluation
requests.show: A feature map stack where random channels/activations are crossed out during training, beside the same network with all features active during evaluation
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that dropout deliberately injects randomness only while training

requests.title: Batch normalization over a minibatch
requests.show: Several samples with the same feature/channel shown together, with mean and standard deviation computed across the minibatch and values rescaled before activation
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that normalization statistics come from the batch during training

requests.title: Residual block with skip connection
requests.show: Input x splits into a learned convolutional path F(x) and an identity shortcut; the two paths are added before continuing
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that the shortcut provides a direct route for information and gradients around the learned block

requests.title: Closed-set classifier on an unknown class
requests.show: A bird and airplane classifier receives three inputs: bird, airplane, and cat; the first two are classified appropriately while the cat is still forced into one known class with high confidence
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that high confidence does not imply the input belongs to the model's known distribution

requests.title: Prediction versus generation
requests.show: Left side shows regression/classification with one input leading to a constrained target; right side shows a text prefix branching into many plausible next-token continuations
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that generation is handled by modeling a probability distribution rather than selecting one permanently fixed answer

requests.title: Vocabulary tokens and encoded sequence
requests.show: A small character vocabulary mapping letters and the $ boundary token to integer IDs, then the name $ada$ shown as its token-ID sequence
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice the distinction between raw characters, tokens, and integer model inputs

requests.title: Character bigram matrix
requests.show: A small heatmap-style matrix where rows are current characters and columns are possible next characters, with darker cells for more likely transitions
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that generation now depends on the previous token rather than a single global distribution

requests.title: Shifted next-token targets with padding
requests.show: Several names of different lengths shown as rectangular input and target tensors, with targets shifted left and padded target cells marked -1/ignored
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice how one raw sequence becomes many next-token learning positions

requests.title: Embedding lookup table
requests.show: Token IDs indexing rows of a learnable embedding matrix and returning dense vectors
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that embeddings are trainable parameters, not fixed handcrafted encodings

requests.title: Query-key-value intuition
requests.show: A sequence of token representations transformed into Q, K, and V rows; one query compares against all keys and then retrieves a weighted mixture of the corresponding values
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should distinguish matching information (Q/K) from retrieved content (V)

requests.title: Dot-product self-attention matrix flow
requests.show: Q multiplied by K-transpose to produce an N×N score matrix, softmax producing row-normalized attention weights, then multiplication by V producing contextualized outputs
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that each output position is a weighted combination of value vectors from the sequence

requests.title: Causal attention matrix
requests.show: A lower-triangular attention grid where each row may attend to itself and earlier tokens but all future-token cells are blocked
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice why the matrix is triangular in an autoregressive decoder

requests.title: Multi-head self-attention
requests.show: One token sequence projected into several parallel attention heads, each producing its own contextual representation, then head outputs concatenated back together
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that multiple heads let the same sequence be analyzed through different learned relationship patterns

requests.title: Token embedding plus positional embedding
requests.show: For each sequence position, a token vector and position vector are added element-wise before entering Transformer blocks
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that content identity and sequence location are represented together

requests.title: BatchNorm versus LayerNorm
requests.show: A small tensor diagram highlighting BatchNorm statistics across examples versus LayerNorm statistics across feature dimensions for each token representation
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that LayerNorm does not depend on other samples in the minibatch in the same way BatchNorm does

requests.title: Encoder-decoder Transformer and cross-attention
requests.show: Source tokens flow through an encoder; decoder tokens use causal self-attention and a separate cross-attention connection into encoder outputs
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should distinguish self-attention inside one sequence from cross-attention between decoder queries and encoder keys/values

requests.title: Tokenization pipeline
requests.show: Raw sentence entering normalization and splitting, then tokens mapped into vocabulary IDs with an unknown-token fallback
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that tokenizer design defines the units the Transformer actually receives

requests.title: Vision Transformer patch pipeline
requests.show: An image divided into a grid of patches; each patch flattened/projected into a token embedding, a CLS token prepended, positional embeddings added, then the sequence passed into Transformer encoder blocks
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that image patches play the same structural role as sequence tokens

requests.lesson_title: From Diffusion Models to Real-World Deep Learning Projects
requests.title: Text generation versus image generation
requests.show: Left side shows next-token probability generation; right side shows spatial image generation; both feed into a shared box labeled learn data distribution and sample new examples
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that different data structures can share the same generative objective

requests.lesson_title: From Diffusion Models to Real-World Deep Learning Projects
requests.title: VAE vs GAN vs diffusion
requests.show: Three side-by-side simplified diagrams: encoder/decoder latent model, generator/discriminator adversarial model, and forward-noise/reverse-denoise diffusion process
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that all generate new samples but learn through different mechanisms

requests.lesson_title: From Diffusion Models to Real-World Deep Learning Projects
requests.title: Forward and reverse diffusion
requests.show: A sequence of the same simple shape progressing from clean to heavily noised left-to-right, with a reverse arrow from noise back to structure
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that training relies on a known corruption process and generation relies on a learned denoising process

requests.lesson_title: From Diffusion Models to Real-World Deep Learning Projects
requests.title: Linear beta noise schedule
requests.show: A plot of beta against timestep increasing from a small starting value to a larger final value
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that the amount of corruption is scheduled rather than arbitrary

requests.lesson_title: From Diffusion Models to Real-World Deep Learning Projects
requests.title: Closed-form diffusion at arbitrary timesteps
requests.show: One clean point-cloud sample branches directly to several different noise levels t=0, 250, 500, 800, 999 without drawing every intermediate transition
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that training can jump directly to a random timestep rather than simulating all earlier steps

requests.lesson_title: From Diffusion Models to Real-World Deep Learning Projects
requests.title: Denoising model input embeddings
requests.show: Noisy x-coordinate, noisy y-coordinate, and timestep each pass through their own embedding transform; the three embeddings are concatenated and fed into an MLP that outputs two noise values
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that the model conditions its prediction on both location and noise level

requests.lesson_title: From Diffusion Models to Real-World Deep Learning Projects
requests.title: Reverse diffusion sampling progression
requests.show: Random 2D points at a late timestep gradually reorganizing through several intermediate snapshots into the PyTorch-logo point-cloud structure
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that generation is iterative rather than a single forward model call

requests.lesson_title: From Diffusion Models to Real-World Deep Learning Projects
requests.title: CT volume as stacked slices and voxels
requests.show: Several grayscale CT slices stacked into a 3D volume, with one small rectangular voxel highlighted and labeled with depth/height/width spacing
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that CT is volumetric data and that voxel dimensions do not have to be cubic

requests.lesson_title: From Diffusion Models to Real-World Deep Learning Projects
requests.title: Lung-cancer project pipeline
requests.show: Raw CT volume flows into data loading, then segmentation/candidate localization, then cropped candidate volumes into a 3D classifier, then candidate results combined for patient-level output
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that one hard problem has been decomposed into smaller interfaces

requests.lesson_title: From Diffusion Models to Real-World Deep Learning Projects
requests.title: Whole CT versus candidate crop
requests.show: Left side shows a large chest CT slice/volume with one tiny highlighted nodule; right side shows a zoomed candidate crop around the nodule
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice how little of the full scan is relevant to the focused classification problem

requests.lesson_title: Combining Data Sources into a Unified Dataset
requests.title: Raw CT data to PyTorch sample
requests.show: Raw .mhd/.raw files and candidate CSV metadata flow through loading, coordinate conversion, cropping, tensor conversion, and finally a training-sample tuple
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that model-ready data is the result of several transformations, not one file-read call

requests.lesson_title: Combining Data Sources into a Unified Dataset
requests.title: Fuzzy matching two nearby annotation centers
requests.show: Two nearly overlapping 3D coordinate points labeled candidate.csv and annotations.csv inside the same nodule-sized region
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that noisy metadata may require domain-aware approximate matching rather than exact equality

requests.lesson_title: Combining Data Sources into a Unified Dataset
requests.title: MetaIO files to CT array
requests.show: A .mhd metadata file and .raw binary file enter SimpleITK and produce one D×H×W NumPy array plus origin/spacing/direction metadata
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that the parser hides file-format complexity but the pipeline still needs to understand the meaning of the loaded data

requests.lesson_title: Combining Data Sources into a Unified Dataset
requests.title: Hounsfield Unit range
requests.show: A horizontal HU scale marking air near -1000, water near 0, soft tissue around intermediate values, and dense bone around +1000, with clipping boundaries highlighted
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice why the chapter limits the working intensity range

requests.lesson_title: Combining Data Sources into a Unified Dataset
requests.title: XYZ patient coordinates versus IRC array coordinates
requests.show: A CT volume shown with one physical patient-space XYZ coordinate system and a separate array-index IRC system, with different origins and axis conventions
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that coordinate conversion is required before indexing the voxel array

requests.lesson_title: Combining Data Sources into a Unified Dataset
requests.title: Candidate crop from CT volume
requests.show: A full 3D CT volume with a small candidate center marker, then a zoomed rectangular 3D crop extracted around that center
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that the classifier receives a focused local volume rather than the complete patient scan

requests.lesson_title: Combining Data Sources into a Unified Dataset
requests.title: LunaDataset sample tuple
requests.show: A 1×32×48×48 candidate tensor plus class tensor, series UID, and IRC center grouped into one Dataset return tuple
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that training data can include both model inputs and metadata useful for debugging/evaluation

requests.lesson_title: Combining Data Sources into a Unified Dataset
requests.title: CT candidate visualization workflow
requests.show: A full CT slice with candidate marker followed by neighboring slices through the extracted crop
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that visual inspection connects metadata, coordinate conversion, and final model input in one sanity check

requests.lesson_title: Training a Classification Model to Detect Suspected Tumors
requests.title: Chapter 13 end-to-end training pipeline
requests.show: LunaDataset feeds DataLoader batches into a 3D classifier; the training branch computes loss, backward, and optimizer step, while the validation branch computes read-only metrics
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that this is the first complete train-and-evaluate loop for the CT project

requests.lesson_title: Training a Classification Model to Detect Suspected Tumors
requests.title: Candidate samples collated into a 3D batch
requests.show: Several C×D×H×W candidate tensors are stacked into an N×C×D×H×W batch by DataLoader
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that DataLoader adds the batch dimension while preserving the single CT-intensity channel

requests.lesson_title: Training a Classification Model to Detect Suspected Tumors
requests.title: DataLoader workers feeding a GPU
requests.show: Multiple CPU worker processes load and prepare batches into a queue while the GPU consumes the previous batch
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that overlapping data preparation with GPU work reduces idle time

requests.lesson_title: Training a Classification Model to Detect Suspected Tumors
requests.title: LunaModel tail-backbone-head architecture
requests.show: Input 3D crop enters BatchNorm3d tail, four repeated convolutional blocks form the backbone, then flattened features enter a linear two-class head
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice the familiar high-level vision-model organization

requests.lesson_title: Training a Classification Model to Detect Suspected Tumors
requests.title: Growing 3D receptive field through two convolutions
requests.show: One deep output voxel traced backward through two 3×3×3 convolution neighborhoods into a larger 5×5×5 source region, followed by 2×2×2 pooling
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that small kernels compose into larger effective receptive fields

requests.lesson_title: Training a Classification Model to Detect Suspected Tumors
requests.title: Training versus validation loop
requests.show: Parallel diagrams show training using train mode, forward, loss, backward, and optimizer step; validation uses eval mode, forward, metrics, and no_grad with no backward/update arrows
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that validation must not modify weights

requests.lesson_title: Training a Classification Model to Detect Suspected Tumors
requests.title: Overall accuracy split into per-class performance
requests.show: One large overall-accuracy bar is decomposed into separate non-nodule and nodule accuracy/loss panels
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice how a strong majority-class score can hide catastrophic minority-class failure

requests.lesson_title: Training a Classification Model to Detect Suspected Tumors
requests.title: TensorBoard training and validation dashboard
requests.show: Several time-series charts for overall loss, positive loss, negative loss, and percent correct with training and validation runs visible together
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that trends expose problems more clearly than isolated epoch numbers

requests.lesson_title: Training a Classification Model to Detect Suspected Tumors
requests.title: Misleading 99.7 percent accuracy under class imbalance
requests.show: A dataset graphic with roughly 99.7 percent negative samples and 0.3 percent positive samples; a classifier predicts every item negative and still receives a 99.7 percent overall accuracy badge while positive recall is zero
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should immediately see why the aggregate score is misleading

requests.lesson_title: Improving Training with Metrics and Augmentation
requests.title: Four binary-classification quadrants
requests.show: A clean 2×2 confusion-grid showing true positive, true negative, false positive, and false negative with nodule/non-nodule examples
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should immediately see that false positives and false negatives are different mistakes with different consequences

requests.lesson_title: Improving Training with Metrics and Augmentation
requests.title: Threshold tradeoff between positives and negatives
requests.show: Overlapping distributions of negative and positive model scores with a movable vertical threshold; arrows show that moving left raises recall while moving right raises precision
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that threshold changes trade one error type for another

requests.lesson_title: Improving Training with Metrics and Augmentation
requests.title: Precision versus recall denominators
requests.show: Two small diagrams highlight TP/(TP+FN) for recall and TP/(TP+FP) for precision using the same TP/FP/FN/TN grid
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that both metrics use TP but answer different questions

requests.lesson_title: Improving Training with Metrics and Augmentation
requests.title: F1 surface over precision and recall
requests.show: A conceptual contour/surface plot where the best values occur when both precision and recall are high and balanced, while regions with one value near zero remain poor
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should see why F1 discourages extreme one-sided behavior

requests.lesson_title: Improving Training with Metrics and Augmentation
requests.title: Gradient tug-of-war under 400-to-1 imbalance
requests.show: A huge group of negative examples pulls model weights strongly toward negative predictions while a tiny positive group pulls in the opposite direction
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should see why random initialization plus extreme imbalance can rapidly collapse to a majority-only solution

requests.lesson_title: Improving Training with Metrics and Augmentation
requests.title: Small false-positive rate on a huge negative class
requests.show: A large block of 54,971 negative samples with only 1 percent highlighted as false positives, placed beside 136 true positive cases; the false-positive group is still several times larger
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice why precision can remain poor despite 99 percent negative accuracy

requests.lesson_title: Improving Training with Metrics and Augmentation
requests.title: Training versus validation positive loss divergence
requests.show: Two curves over epochs: training positive loss falls toward zero while validation positive loss turns upward
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should identify the point where more training begins to harm generalization

requests.lesson_title: Improving Training with Metrics and Augmentation
requests.title: One nodule producing many augmented views
requests.show: One original 3D candidate crop branches into mirrored, shifted, scaled, rotated, and noisy variants, all keeping the same positive label
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that augmentation changes appearance while preserving the task-relevant identity

requests.lesson_title: Improving Training with Metrics and Augmentation
requests.title: Valid CT rotation plane
requests.show: A 3D CT candidate crop with the in-plane X-Y axes highlighted and a rotation arrow around the head-foot axis, while the anisotropic slice-depth axis is marked as special
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should see why rotation is restricted instead of freely rotating across all 3D axes

requests.lesson_title: Improving Training with Metrics and Augmentation
requests.title: TensorBoard comparison of augmentation runs
requests.show: Multiple validation curves for balanced baseline, rotation, noise, and fully augmented models across recall, precision, F1, and positive loss
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that different augmentations affect precision and recall differently and that full augmentation reduces overfitting

requests.lesson_title: Using Segmentation to Find Suspected Nodules
requests.title: Multi-stage CT pipeline with segmentation before classification
requests.show: Raw CT slice enters a segmentation model, candidate regions are extracted, then passed into the existing classifier
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that segmentation answers where while classification answers what

requests.lesson_title: Using Segmentation to Find Suspected Nodules
requests.title: Semantic segmentation vs instance segmentation vs object detection
requests.show: One medical-style image shown three times: semantic mask labels all tumor pixels as one class, instance segmentation gives separate IDs to separate tumors, and object detection uses bounding boxes
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should distinguish pixel-level categories, object identities, and bounding boxes

requests.lesson_title: Using Segmentation to Find Suspected Nodules
requests.title: Classification versus segmentation output
requests.show: Same input image feeds two models; classifier returns one class vector, segmenter returns an image-sized mask
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that segmentation must preserve location information throughout the network

requests.lesson_title: Using Segmentation to Find Suspected Nodules
requests.title: SAM architecture
requests.show: Input image enters a ViT image encoder; point/box/mask prompts enter a prompt encoder; both streams meet in a mask decoder that outputs masks and confidence
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should understand the three-component division of SAM

requests.lesson_title: Using Segmentation to Find Suspected Nodules
requests.title: Binary segmentation mask
requests.show: Original image beside a black-and-white mask where the target object is white and background is black
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should see that every output pixel corresponds spatially to the input

requests.lesson_title: Using Segmentation to Find Suspected Nodules
requests.title: Point-prompt segmentation
requests.show: Image with one marked point inside an object and three candidate masks produced around that region
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that the prompt guides which part of the image SAM should segment

requests.lesson_title: Using Segmentation to Find Suspected Nodules
requests.title: Extracting one 2D CT slice from a 3D volume
requests.show: CT volume shown as stacked slices with one highlighted slice at the candidate depth; highlighted slice is pulled out as a 2D image
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should see the adaptation required for a 2D model

requests.lesson_title: Using Segmentation to Find Suspected Nodules
requests.title: Fine-tuning dataset layout
requests.show: Folder tree with CT images, mask images, and metadata.jsonl; one metadata record links series UID and center IRC to matching image and mask paths
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should understand the pairing and traceability structure

requests.lesson_title: Using Segmentation to Find Suspected Nodules
requests.title: SAM as mask teacher and SegFormer as deployable segmenter
requests.show: Known point prompts plus CT slices go through SAM to create training masks; those image-mask pairs train SegFormer; trained SegFormer later receives only a CT image
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should see why the second model removes the prompt requirement

requests.lesson_title: Using Segmentation to Find Suspected Nodules
requests.title: SegFormer encoder-decoder overview
requests.show: CT image passes through transformer-style encoder stages at multiple scales, then a lightweight decoder fuses features and outputs a two-class pixel mask
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should understand that segmentation retains multi-scale spatial information rather than collapsing to one class vector

requests.lesson_title: Using Segmentation to Find Suspected Nodules
requests.title: Fine-tuning train and validation loss curves
requests.show: Two TensorBoard-style curves for SegFormer training and validation loss both trending downward
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should inspect whether validation follows training rather than diverging upward

requests.lesson_title: Using Segmentation to Find Suspected Nodules
requests.title: SegFormer inference comparison
requests.show: Three panels: CT slice, target mask, predicted segmentation map
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should visually compare whether the predicted region overlaps the target nodule area

requests.title: Transformer evolution timeline
requests.show: A simple chronological timeline showing the 2017 Transformer paper, ULMFiT, GPT, BERT, and the subsequent expansion of transformer models
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that modern transformer NLP emerged from the combination of a new architecture and practical transfer-learning methods

requests.title: RNN unrolled through time
requests.show: A recurrent network shown both as a feedback loop and as an unrolled sequence of hidden states h1, h2, h3, h4
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that each step depends on the state produced by the previous step

requests.title: Encoder-decoder bottleneck
requests.show: An RNN encoder reading several input tokens into a final hidden-state vector, followed by an RNN decoder generating output tokens one at a time
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that the single final encoder state forms a narrow information bottleneck between input and output

requests.title: Attention alignment matrix
requests.show: A heatmap with source-language tokens on one axis and target-language tokens on the other, with darker cells showing stronger attention weights
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that strong cells can connect corresponding words even when their positions differ between languages

requests.title: Transformer self-attention overview
requests.show: A simplified Transformer encoder-decoder diagram showing self-attention blocks followed by feed-forward networks, without detailed equations
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that recurrence is removed and attention is the main mechanism connecting token information

requests.title: Training from scratch versus transfer learning
requests.show: Side-by-side diagram comparing a task model trained only on a small labeled dataset with a pretrained model adapted to that same downstream task
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that transfer learning reuses general knowledge instead of relearning everything from the task dataset

requests.title: ULMFiT three-stage workflow
requests.show: A three-step flow labeled pretraining, domain adaptation, and task fine-tuning
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice how a broadly pretrained language model is progressively specialized

requests.title: Hugging Face ecosystem map
requests.show: A simple hub-and-spoke diagram connecting the Hub with Transformers, Tokenizers, Datasets, and Accelerate
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that a practical NLP workflow is an ecosystem of interoperating tools rather than only a model architecture

requests.title: Transformer encoder-decoder overview
requests.show: A clean diagram showing input tokens entering an encoder stack, encoder outputs feeding a decoder stack, and the decoder generating output tokens one by one
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that the encoder processes the source sequence while the decoder produces the target sequence autoregressively

requests.title: Transformer encoder layer zoom
requests.show: One encoder block showing multi-head self-attention, residual connection, layer normalization, feed-forward network, and the second residual/normalization path
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that attention and the feed-forward network are separate stages and that the hidden dimension is preserved across the block

requests.title: Contextualized meaning of flies
requests.show: Two short sentences containing the word 'flies', with attention links from 'flies' to context words such as 'time' and 'arrow' in one sentence and 'fruit' and 'banana' in the other
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that the same token can receive different contextual representations depending on surrounding words

requests.title: Scaled dot-product attention pipeline
requests.show: A left-to-right diagram with Q and K entering a dot product, division by sqrt(d_k), softmax producing attention weights, and multiplication with V producing the output
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that Q and K determine relevance while V supplies the information that is actually aggregated

requests.title: Multi-head attention
requests.show: One input sequence splitting into several parallel attention heads, each with its own Q/K/V projections, followed by concatenation and a final linear projection
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that heads process the same sequence in parallel but can learn different attention patterns

requests.title: Pre-norm versus post-norm
requests.show: Side-by-side encoder-block diagrams showing where layer normalization sits relative to the residual connection in pre-norm and post-norm arrangements
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should focus on the ordering difference rather than memorizing every arrow

requests.title: Token plus position embeddings
requests.show: A sequence showing token embeddings and position embeddings being added element-wise before entering the encoder stack
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that attention receives both token identity information and sequence-order information

requests.title: Transformer decoder with causal mask
requests.show: A decoder layer showing masked self-attention first and encoder-decoder attention second, plus a small triangular attention mask
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that self-attention cannot see future target positions while cross-attention can read encoder outputs

requests.title: Transformer family tree
requests.show: A three-branch family tree with encoder-only, decoder-only, and encoder-decoder at the top, then representative models from the chapter under each branch
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should use the diagram to categorize models by architecture rather than memorizing an unstructured list of names

requests.title: IOB2 named entity labeling
requests.show: A short sentence with tokens shown in boxes and colored labels underneath for B-PER, I-PER, B-ORG, B-LOC, and O
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that B marks the start of an entity span, I continues it, and O means the token is not part of an entity

requests.title: Zero-shot cross-lingual transfer
requests.show: A flow diagram where one multilingual XLM-R model is fine-tuned on labeled German NER data and then evaluated directly on French, Italian, and English without target-language fine-tuning
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that the task labels stay the same while the language changes

requests.title: Tokenizer pipeline
requests.show: A four-stage pipeline labeled normalization, pretokenization, subword tokenizer model, and postprocessing, using one short multilingual-friendly example
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that subword splitting is only one stage of the complete tokenization process

requests.title: Sequence classification versus token classification
requests.show: Side-by-side diagrams: sequence classification uses one pooled representation for one label, while NER sends every token hidden state through the same classifier to produce one entity label per token
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice the difference between one prediction per sequence and one prediction per token

requests.title: Word-to-subword NER label alignment
requests.show: A word-level NER sequence above a subword-tokenized sequence, with arrows from each original word to its subwords; first subwords receive the real label and later subwords/special tokens receive -100/IGN
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that tokenization changes sequence length, so labels must be explicitly realigned before training

requests.title: NER error-analysis dashboard
requests.show: A conceptual figure containing three panels: highest-loss tokens, a normalized confusion matrix highlighting B-ORG versus I-ORG confusion, and one high-loss sequence with token labels and predictions
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that useful error analysis moves from aggregate score to class-level, token-level, and example-level investigation

requests.title: Zero-shot versus target-language fine-tuning curve
requests.show: A learning curve with number of French labeled training examples on the x-axis, F1 on the y-axis, a horizontal line for German-to-French zero-shot performance, and an increasing line for direct French fine-tuning
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that the preferred strategy can change as labeled target-language data becomes available

requests.title: Multilingual fine-tuning comparison
requests.show: A simple grouped bar chart comparing German-only, each-language, and all-language fine-tuning across de, fr, it, and en using the chapter's F1 values
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that joint multilingual training improves the overall balance across languages in this experiment

requests.title: Autoregressive text generation loop
requests.show: A step-by-step diagram showing prompt -> language model -> next-token probabilities -> selected token -> append token to prompt -> repeat
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that one new token is chosen per decoding step and the generated token becomes part of the next input

requests.title: Beam search with two beams
requests.show: A small search tree showing a prompt expanding into candidate tokens, then multiple second-step candidates, with only the two highest-scoring partial sequences retained after each step
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that beam search explores several paths rather than committing to one greedy continuation immediately

requests.title: Temperature changes token probabilities
requests.show: Three probability distributions over the same candidate tokens for low, medium, and high temperature, with low temperature sharply concentrated and high temperature flatter
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that temperature changes the distribution rather than directly specifying which token must be selected

requests.title: Top-k versus top-p sampling
requests.show: A sorted next-token probability distribution with one fixed vertical cutoff illustrating top-k and one cumulative-probability threshold illustrating top-p
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that top-k keeps a fixed number of tokens while top-p adapts the number of candidates to the shape of the distribution

requests.title: Complete text-generation decoding workflow
requests.show: A single flowchart from prompt and tokenizer through model logits, probability adjustments, decoding choices, selected token, and the feedback loop into the next generation step
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should see clearly that the model and decoder are separate parts of the generation system

requests.title: Summarization as sequence-to-sequence learning
requests.show: A long document entering an encoder-decoder transformer and a short summary coming out, with arrows showing compression from source sequence to target sequence
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that the output is a newly generated sequence rather than a fixed class label

requests.title: Long-document truncation problem
requests.show: A long article represented as many text blocks, a model context window covering only the beginning, and later blocks faded or cut off
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that truncation can remove information that may be important for the final summary

requests.title: Comparison of summarization model families
requests.show: A compact four-column visual for GPT-2, T5, BART, and PEGASUS showing decoder-only prompting for GPT-2 and encoder-decoder summarization for the other models, with their pretraining idea summarized beneath each
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that models differ both in architecture and in how closely their training objective matches summarization

requests.title: BLEU versus ROUGE intuition
requests.show: Two overlapping sets labeled generated n-grams and reference n-grams, with BLEU highlighting the generated side as precision-oriented and ROUGE highlighting the reference side as recall-oriented
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should understand the directional difference without memorizing formulas

requests.title: Domain shift from news to dialogue
requests.show: A side-by-side visual showing a structured news article with headline-style summary on the left and an informal chat dialogue with abstractive conversational summary on the right
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that the task name is the same but the data distribution and desired output style are different

requests.title: Teacher forcing in an encoder-decoder model
requests.show: A training diagram where the encoder receives the source dialogue and the decoder receives the gold target summary shifted right by one token, with arrows showing next-token prediction at each decoder position
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that the decoder sees previous correct target tokens during training but never the current/future target token it is predicting

requests.title: Hierarchical long-document summarization
requests.show: A long document split into several chunks, each producing a short partial summary, followed by a second summarization stage combining those partial summaries
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should see one conceptual alternative to simply truncating a long document

requests.title: Transformer production optimization overview
requests.show: A large accurate transformer on the left and four optimization paths labeled distillation, quantization, ONNX Runtime, and pruning leading toward a smaller/faster deployment model
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that several techniques can be combined rather than treated as mutually exclusive choices

requests.title: In-scope versus out-of-scope intent detection
requests.show: Three small chat examples: one correctly routed in-scope query, one out-of-scope query incorrectly forced into a known intent, and one out-of-scope query correctly sent to a fallback response
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that production classification includes safe handling of unknown requests, not only predicting known intents

requests.title: Teacher-student knowledge distillation
requests.show: One input branching into a large teacher and smaller student; teacher produces soft class probabilities, student produces its own probabilities, and the final student loss combines label loss with teacher-student distribution matching
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that the teacher guides training but is not needed for student inference after training

requests.title: Hard labels versus soft teacher probabilities
requests.show: Three side-by-side bar charts: one-hot hard label, normal teacher softmax, and temperature-softened teacher probabilities
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that higher temperature reveals relative probabilities among non-winning classes

requests.title: FP32 to INT8 quantization
requests.show: A continuous number line of floating-point weight values mapped onto a smaller set of discrete INT8 levels using a scale and zero point
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that quantization saves precision by grouping nearby floating-point values into shared integer levels

requests.title: Simplified ONNX computational graph
requests.show: A small directed graph of model operators such as input, MatMul, Add, LayerNorm, and output, shown as connected nodes
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that ONNX describes the inference computation as a graph of standardized operations rather than a high-level Python model class

requests.title: Production optimization benchmark trade-off
requests.show: A scatter plot with average latency on the x-axis and accuracy on the y-axis, bubble size representing model size, containing the BERT baseline, distilled model, quantized model, ORT model, and ORT-quantized model using the chapter's benchmark values
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that the optimized models move toward lower latency and smaller size without a large accuracy penalty

requests.title: Dense network versus pruned sparse network
requests.show: Two small neural network diagrams side by side, one with dense connections and one with many connections removed
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that pruning reduces the number of active nonzero connections rather than merely reducing numerical precision

requests.title: Magnitude versus movement pruning
requests.show: A side-by-side conceptual comparison where magnitude pruning ranks weights by absolute size and movement pruning ranks them using learned movement/importance scores during fine-tuning
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should understand that the two methods answer 'which weights matter?' using different signals

requests.title: Two-stage question answering system
requests.show: A question enters a retriever that selects relevant documents, then a reader extracts an answer span from one of those documents
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that document retrieval and answer extraction are separate problems in a practical QA system

requests.title: Extractive QA span-classification head
requests.show: Question and context tokens enter a transformer encoder; each token hidden state feeds a small QA head that produces start and end logits, with the selected answer span highlighted inside the context
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that the answer is defined by two token positions

requests.title: Sliding window for long-context QA
requests.show: A long token sequence with the question shown separately and several overlapping context windows beneath it; the answer span lies near a boundary but is fully captured in at least one window
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice why overlap/stride is necessary instead of simple truncation

requests.title: Retriever-reader QA architecture
requests.show: Question -> document store -> retriever -> top-k documents -> optional reranker -> reader -> answer candidates, with clear separation of retrieval and reading stages
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that retrieval reduces the amount of text the expensive reader must process

requests.title: DPR bi-encoder architecture
requests.show: A question enters one BERT-like encoder and a passage enters another; each produces a dense vector and their similarity determines relevance
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that the question and passage are encoded separately, which enables efficient retrieval over many stored passage vectors

requests.title: QA domain-adaptation path
requests.show: A three-stage pipeline from pretrained MiniLM to SQuAD fine-tuning to SubjQA fine-tuning, contrasted with a shorter direct MiniLM-to-SubjQA path that performs worse in the chapter
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice the benefit of task transfer before small-domain adaptation

requests.title: QA component versus end-to-end evaluation
requests.show: A diagram with separate metric boxes under retriever (Recall@k), reader (EM/F1 with gold contexts), and full system (end-to-end EM/F1 + latency)
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that every layer needs its own evaluation as well as a final system-level evaluation

requests.title: RAG architecture
requests.show: Question -> dense retriever -> top-k passages -> sequence-to-sequence generator -> generated answer, with the retrieval stage visually connected to generation
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that RAG grounds generation in retrieved external documents rather than generating from the language model alone

requests.title: QA hierarchy of needs
requests.show: A three-level pyramid with retrieval/search at the base, extractive QA in the middle, and generative QA/RAG at the top
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that strong retrieval is foundational and generative QA should build on a reliable evidence pipeline

requests.lesson_title: Dealing with Few to No Labels
requests.title: Low-label method decision tree
requests.show: A decision tree beginning with 'Do you have labeled data?', then branching by amount of labeled data and availability of unlabeled data toward zero-shot, few-shot/embedding methods, domain adaptation/UDA/UST, or ordinary fine-tuning
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that the correct method depends on the available supervision, not on which technique sounds most advanced

requests.lesson_title: Dealing with Few to No Labels
requests.title: NLI zero-shot classification
requests.show: One issue text acts as the premise and branches into several hypotheses such as 'This example is about new model', '...tokenization', and '...documentation'; each receives an entailment score
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that no task-specific classifier is trained; class names are expressed directly in natural language

requests.lesson_title: Dealing with Few to No Labels
requests.title: Text data augmentation examples
requests.show: One source sentence branching into synonym replacement, random insertion, random swap, random deletion, and back-translation variants
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that augmentation attempts to vary surface form while preserving the original class label

requests.lesson_title: Dealing with Few to No Labels
requests.title: Embedding nearest-neighbor classifier
requests.show: Several labeled text points represented in embedding space, a new query point, and lines connecting it to its nearest neighbors whose labels are aggregated
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that the pretrained representation does the heavy lifting without updating model weights

requests.lesson_title: Dealing with Few to No Labels
requests.title: FAISS clustered vector index
requests.show: A 2D embedding space partitioned into several regions around centroid points, with one query vector first matched to a centroid and then compared with vectors inside that region
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice how partitioning avoids comparing the query with every stored embedding

requests.lesson_title: Dealing with Few to No Labels
requests.title: Domain-adaptive language-model training
requests.show: A pipeline from general BERT pretraining to continued masked-language-model training on many unlabeled GitHub issues, then to a small supervised classifier
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that unlabeled domain text is used before the task-specific fine-tuning stage

requests.lesson_title: Dealing with Few to No Labels
requests.title: Unsupervised data augmentation consistency training
requests.show: One unlabeled example branches into original and augmented text; both enter the same model and their output distributions are connected by a consistency/KL loss, alongside a normal supervised loss from labeled examples
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that UDA extracts a training signal from unlabeled text without inventing hard labels for every example

requests.lesson_title: Dealing with Few to No Labels
requests.title: Uncertainty-aware self-training loop
requests.show: Labeled data trains a teacher; the teacher predicts pseudo-labels with uncertainty estimation on unlabeled data; selected pseudo-labeled examples train a student; the student becomes the next teacher and the loop repeats
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice both the iterative teacher-student cycle and the role of uncertainty in selecting pseudo-labels

requests.title: Three transformer research directions
requests.show: A central transformer branching into three paths labeled scaling, efficient attention, and multimodal/beyond-text learning
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that the chapter treats these as distinct but complementary ways of extending transformer capability

requests.title: Scaling laws on log-log axes
requests.show: Three small charts showing test loss decreasing smoothly as compute, dataset size, and model size increase, with approximately straight trends on log-log axes
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice the similar power-law shape across N, D, and C

requests.title: Scaling challenge stack
requests.show: A vertical stack labeled infrastructure, cost, dataset curation, model evaluation, and deployment surrounding a very large language model
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that scaling affects the entire ML lifecycle, not only training

requests.title: Quadratic self-attention growth
requests.show: Attention matrices for short, medium, and long sequences shown growing from small square to much larger square, with n² highlighted
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that doubling sequence length roughly quadruples the pairwise attention-score space

requests.title: Atomic sparse attention patterns
requests.show: Five small attention matrices showing global, band, dilated, random, and block-local patterns using filled cells for calculated scores and blank cells for skipped scores
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should compare how each pattern reduces the number of pairwise calculations

requests.title: Longformer and BigBird compound sparsity
requests.show: Two attention matrices side by side: Longformer showing local band plus global rows/columns, and BigBird adding random sparse links
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that practical efficient-attention models combine multiple sparsity patterns

requests.title: Standard versus linearized attention
requests.show: A side-by-side computational diagram: standard attention explicitly forms a QK^T matrix, while linearized attention applies feature maps and rearranged matrix products without materializing the full pairwise matrix
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should focus on the structural difference rather than the detailed algebra

requests.title: Vision Transformer patch pipeline
requests.show: An image divided into equal square patches, each patch converted to an embedding, position embeddings added, then all patch tokens entering a transformer encoder
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice the analogy between image patches and text tokens

requests.title: TAPAS table question answering
requests.show: A small table, a natural-language question above it, selected cells highlighted, and an optional aggregator such as SUM or COUNT producing the final answer
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that answering may require both cell selection and aggregation

requests.title: wav2vec 2.0 speech-recognition pipeline
requests.show: An audio waveform entering convolutional feature extraction, then transformer context layers, then producing a text transcription
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice the combination of low-level audio feature processing and transformer-based contextual representation learning

requests.title: Multimodal document understanding with LayoutLM
requests.show: A scanned invoice with text boxes and coordinates feeding text, visual, and layout embeddings into one transformer
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that document understanding combines what the text says with where it appears and what the page looks like

requests.title: CLIP contrastive learning
requests.show: A batch of images and captions encoded into vectors with a similarity matrix; matching image-caption pairs highlighted along the diagonal and mismatched pairs shown off-diagonal
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that training rewards matching pairs and separates mismatches

requests.title: Fine-tuning versus training from scratch
