requests.show: A decision diagram comparing a small domain dataset flowing into pretrained-model fine-tuning versus a massive distinct domain corpus flowing into custom tokenizer training and fresh model pretraining
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that training from scratch requires both much more data and much more compute

requests.title: Corpus-to-model behavior pipeline
requests.show: A large dataset containing useful patterns plus bias/noise/copyright/privacy risks feeding pretraining, followed by a model whose generated outputs reflect both the useful and undesirable corpus patterns
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that corpus choices propagate into model behavior

requests.title: Memory mapping versus streaming
requests.show: Two side-by-side workflows: memory mapping shows a large local Arrow/cache file accessed through small memory windows, while streaming shows remote compressed files sending only the current batch to RAM
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that both avoid loading the complete corpus into memory

requests.title: Byte-level BPE for Python code
requests.show: A short indented Python function mapped first into byte-aware symbols for spaces and newlines, then frequent byte combinations merged into larger BPE tokens
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that indentation and line breaks remain represented rather than being discarded

requests.title: Generic versus code-trained tokenizer
requests.show: The same Python function tokenized by a generic GPT-2 tokenizer and by the custom CodeParrot tokenizer, with token counts shown below
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that the domain tokenizer groups indentation and common code patterns more efficiently

requests.title: Three pretraining objectives for code
requests.show: Three side-by-side mini diagrams: CLM predicts future code with a decoder, MLM reconstructs masked code with an encoder, and seq2seq maps code to comments or comments to code with an encoder-decoder
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that task objective determines the appropriate architecture

requests.title: Constant-length CLM preprocessing
requests.show: Several code files of different lengths are tokenized and concatenated with EOS markers, then sliced into equal 1024-token chunks
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that file boundaries are preserved with EOS tokens while training sequences stay fully packed

requests.title: Four-GPU data parallel training
requests.show: A main data stream splits into four batches sent to four GPUs, each GPU contains the same model, local gradients flow into an averaging/reduce operation, and the averaged gradient is sent back to all four model copies
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that data is divided while each GPU maintains a synchronized copy of the model

requests.title: Training loss and perplexity curves
requests.show: Two conceptual curves over processed tokens showing training loss and validation perplexity decreasing, with separate small-model and large-model curves
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that the larger model improves faster with respect to tokens processed even though the wall-clock training run is longer

requests.title: Functional evaluation for generated code
requests.show: A programming prompt branches into several generated code candidates; each candidate runs through the same unit-test suite, producing pass/fail results; the final metric is based on functional success rather than text overlap
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that semantic correctness of code is best checked by execution

requests.title: Transformer text-classification pipeline
requests.show: A simple flow from raw tweet to Dataset processing, tokenizer, DistilBERT, classification output, and prediction on new text
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that text must pass through data preparation and tokenization before the transformer can classify it

requests.title: Emotion class distribution
requests.show: A horizontal bar chart showing that some emotion classes are much more frequent than others
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice why class imbalance changes how raw accuracy should be interpreted

requests.title: Tweet length distribution by emotion
requests.show: Boxplots of words per tweet grouped by emotion, all well below the DistilBERT input limit
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that these tweets are short enough that truncation is unlikely to remove important content

requests.title: Padding and attention mask
requests.show: Two tokenized sequences of different lengths padded to the same width, with an attention mask showing 1 for real tokens and 0 for padding
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should understand that padding fixes tensor shape while the mask prevents PAD positions from being treated as meaningful text

requests.title: Feature-extraction architecture
requests.show: DistilBERT encoder shown as frozen, producing a hidden-state vector that is passed to a separate classifier such as logistic regression
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that only the final classifier is trained while the transformer body stays unchanged

requests.title: UMAP projection of emotion hidden states
requests.show: A 2D projection with separate panels or colors for sadness, joy, love, anger, fear, and surprise
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that some emotions form similar regions while a 2D projection is only a simplified view of the original 768-dimensional space

requests.title: Feature-based confusion matrix
requests.show: A normalized confusion matrix for the logistic-regression classifier using DistilBERT hidden states
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that the diagonal represents correct predictions while off-diagonal cells reveal specific class confusions

requests.title: Fine-tuning architecture
requests.show: DistilBERT encoder connected to a classification head with both parts marked trainable and an arrow from loss/backpropagation updating the full model
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should contrast this with feature extraction, where the encoder is frozen

requests.title: Emotion prediction probabilities
requests.show: A bar chart showing the model's class probabilities for a new positive tweet, with joy clearly highest
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that inference produces scores across classes and the final predicted class comes from the strongest score

requests.lesson_title: An Introduction to Large Language Models
requests.title: Language AI landscape
requests.show: A simple map showing Language AI as the broader field, with branches for representation, classification, clustering, semantic search/retrieval, translation, and generation/LLMs
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that LLMs are one important part of Language AI rather than the entire field

requests.lesson_title: An Introduction to Large Language Models
requests.title: Recent history of Language AI
requests.show: A timeline-style figure showing the progression from bag-of-words to word2vec, sequence models with attention, Transformers, BERT, GPT, and modern LLM systems
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that modern LLMs emerged through a sequence of improvements in representation and context handling

requests.lesson_title: An Introduction to Large Language Models
requests.title: Bag-of-words pipeline
requests.show: A four-stage diagram: two input sentences → tokenization → combined vocabulary → count vectors
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that the method converts text into numbers by counting tokens, but does not encode rich meaning or context

requests.lesson_title: An Introduction to Large Language Models
requests.title: Semantic embedding space
requests.show: A 2D conceptual projection with related words grouped close together and unrelated words farther apart
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that semantic similarity is represented by geometric closeness, while remembering that real embeddings usually have many dimensions

requests.lesson_title: An Introduction to Large Language Models
requests.title: Attention in translation
requests.show: An encoder-decoder translation diagram with visible attention links between source and target words, including a strong link between “llamas” and its translated form
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that the decoder can focus on the most relevant source token instead of relying only on one compressed context vector

requests.lesson_title: An Introduction to Large Language Models
requests.title: Transformer encoder-decoder mental model
requests.show: A simplified Transformer diagram with stacked encoder blocks on the left, stacked decoder blocks on the right, self-attention inside both, encoder-to-decoder attention, and a mask over future decoder positions
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice the difference between encoding the full input and autoregressively generating output without looking ahead

requests.lesson_title: An Introduction to Large Language Models
requests.title: BERT versus GPT architecture
requests.show: A side-by-side conceptual diagram showing BERT as an encoder-only stack producing representations and GPT as a decoder-only stack producing text token by token
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that both are Transformer-based but optimized for different primary roles

requests.lesson_title: An Introduction to Large Language Models
requests.title: LLM training paradigm
requests.show: A two-stage diagram contrasting traditional one-step task training with LLM pretraining on broad text followed by fine-tuning/post-training for a narrower task or instruction following
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that expensive general pretraining is reused, while adaptation happens afterward

requests.lesson_title: An Introduction to Large Language Models
requests.title: Hosted API versus local open model
requests.show: A side-by-side diagram: application → external provider API → hosted proprietary model, versus application → locally hosted open model on user hardware
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice the trade-off between convenience/provider-managed compute and local control/privacy/hardware responsibility

requests.title: Tokens-to-embeddings overview
requests.show: A left-to-right diagram showing raw text being split into tokens, tokens mapped to integer IDs, IDs mapped to embedding vectors, and vectors passed into a language model
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that tokenization and embedding are separate stages and that token IDs are identifiers rather than semantic vectors

requests.title: Visible text versus token pieces
requests.show: Show one sentence with colored token boundaries, including at least one full-word token, one split word such as apolog + izing, punctuation as its own token, and a special token
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that tokens can be words, subwords, punctuation, or control symbols

requests.title: Tokenizer input-output pipeline
requests.show: A diagram showing prompt text → tokenizer → token IDs → generative model → old plus newly generated token IDs → tokenizer decode → readable text
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that the model communicates through numerical token IDs on both the input and output sides

requests.title: Word vs subword vs character vs byte tokenization
requests.show: Use the same short input and show four parallel rows demonstrating how it would be segmented as whole words, subwords, individual characters, and bytes
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should compare sequence length, vocabulary flexibility, and the ability to handle unseen text

requests.title: Comparison of real tokenizer behavior
requests.show: A compact comparison graphic using one mixed input with English capitalization, emoji/non-English text, code indentation, and numbers, showing that BERT-like, GPT-like, and code-focused tokenizers preserve and split information differently
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that tokenizer choices affect case, unknown symbols, whitespace, number segmentation, and sequence length

requests.title: Vocabulary embedding matrix
requests.show: Show a tokenizer vocabulary column with token IDs pointing to rows in a matrix where each row contains a dense vector
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that every vocabulary token has a learned vector and that the token ID acts as the lookup key

requests.title: Static versus contextual token embedding
requests.show: Show the word “bank” appearing in a financial sentence and a river sentence; start from the same token-level lookup concept and end with two different contextual vectors
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that the language model changes a token's representation according to surrounding context

requests.title: From token IDs to contextual embeddings
requests.show: Show “Hello world” becoming [CLS], Hello, world, [SEP], then token IDs, then raw embedding vectors entering the language model, then four contextual output vectors of width 384
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should connect sequence length with token positions and understand what the [1, 4, 384] output shape represents

requests.title: Sentence-to-vector embedding
requests.show: Show a complete sentence entering a text embedding model and emerging as one vector, followed by three example application branches: semantic search, categorization, and RAG retrieval
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice the difference between many per-token vectors and one vector representing a whole text

requests.title: Word2vec sliding window
requests.show: Show a short sentence with one center word highlighted and two neighboring words on each side inside a sliding window; draw positive training pairs from the center to each neighbor
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice how ordinary running text is converted into many word-pair training examples

requests.title: Positive and negative word2vec pairs
requests.show: Two groups of word pairs: genuine context neighbors labeled 1 and sampled unrelated pairs labeled 0, feeding a small neural network
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that embeddings improve because the model learns to separate observed contextual relationships from negative samples

requests.title: Playlist-to-song-embeddings recommender
requests.show: Show playlists as sequences of song IDs feeding a Word2Vec-style model, producing one vector per song, followed by nearest-neighbor lookup that returns similar songs
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that the same algorithmic idea used for word context can model item similarity from playlist co-occurrence

requests.title: Autoregressive token generation loop
requests.show: Show an initial prompt entering the model, one output token being selected, that token appended to the prompt, and the enlarged sequence entering the model again for the next step
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that generation is an iterative loop rather than one operation that writes the whole answer at once

requests.title: One Transformer forward pass
requests.show: Show tokenizer → token embeddings → stacked Transformer decoder blocks → final hidden vectors → LM head → score for every vocabulary token
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that the Transformer does not directly output a word; the LM head converts a hidden representation into vocabulary-wide next-token scores

requests.title: LM head vocabulary scoring
requests.show: Show one final hidden vector entering the LM head and expanding into a ranked list of candidate vocabulary tokens with scores, with “Paris” highlighted as the chosen candidate
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice the dimensional jump from one hidden vector to one score per vocabulary entry

requests.title: Parallel token processing streams
requests.show: Show several input token embeddings entering parallel vertical streams through the same stack of Transformer blocks, with attention links connecting token positions
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice both parallel per-position processing and the cross-position interaction introduced by attention

requests.title: KV cache generation comparison
requests.show: Side-by-side diagram of generation without cache repeatedly recalculating all previous token streams versus generation with cached keys/values where only the new token stream requires fresh computation
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that caching avoids duplicated attention work for previous positions

requests.title: Simplified Transformer block
requests.show: Show input vectors entering self-attention, then a feedforward/MLP stage, then output vectors continuing to the next Transformer block
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should remember attention as contextual information mixing and the feedforward network as per-position transformation/processing

requests.title: Attention intuition with pronoun reference
requests.show: Show “The dog chased the squirrel because it” with the current token “it” highlighted and attention links of different strengths to earlier words, especially dog and squirrel
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that attention lets the current representation incorporate information from relevant earlier positions

requests.title: Query-key-value projection
requests.show: Show the same set of token input vectors branching through three learned projection matrices W_Q, W_K, and W_V to create query, key, and value representations
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that Q, K, and V are different learned views of the same underlying token representations

requests.title: Two-step attention calculation
requests.show: First panel shows current query compared with keys to create relevance weights; second panel multiplies those weights by value vectors and sums them into one output vector
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should connect query/key interaction with scoring and values with information transfer

requests.title: Multi-head attention
requests.show: Show one input sequence branching into several parallel attention heads, each with different attention patterns, then recombining into a single output
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that multi-head attention repeats the same core mechanism in parallel with different learned projections

requests.title: Full versus local attention
requests.show: Show two triangular decoder-attention grids: one where each position can see all previous positions, and one where each position sees only a recent local window
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice the efficiency-versus-context tradeoff

requests.title: MHA vs MQA vs GQA
requests.show: Three side-by-side diagrams showing multi-head attention with unique Q/K/V per head, multi-query attention with unique Q but one shared K/V set, and grouped-query attention with unique queries and several shared K/V groups
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should understand exactly what is being shared in each design

requests.title: Flash Attention memory intuition
requests.show: Show a GPU diagram with slower/larger HBM and faster/smaller SRAM, comparing inefficient repeated data movement with a tiled/reuse-oriented attention computation
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that Flash Attention targets memory movement and execution efficiency rather than changing what attention conceptually means

requests.title: Original versus modern Transformer block
requests.show: Side-by-side simplified diagrams showing the original attention + feedforward block with normalization/residual structure and a newer block with pre-normalization, RMSNorm-style labels, grouped-query attention, and modern feedforward activation
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that the skeleton remains recognizable while important implementation details evolve

requests.title: Sequence packing
requests.show: Show several short documents packed into one fixed-length training context with boundaries between documents and little padding at the end
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice why packing improves space utilization and why position handling must respect document boundaries

requests.title: RoPE placement in attention
requests.show: Show query and key projections followed by a rotary positional transformation before Q×K relevance scoring; values remain on the information-combination path
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that RoPE injects position into Q and K immediately before attention relevance scoring

requests.title: Complete next-token generation pipeline
requests.show: A detailed left-to-right or top-to-bottom diagram showing text → tokenizer → IDs → embeddings → positional handling → repeated Transformer blocks containing attention and MLP → last hidden vector → LM head → vocabulary scores → decoding → selected token → append to context → repeat, with KV cache shown beside attention
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should be able to use this figure as the final mental model for the entire chapter

requests.title: Text classification overview
requests.show: Show several example text inputs flowing into a language model/classifier and emerging as labels such as Positive, Negative, Billing Issue, and Shipping Issue
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that classification converts unstructured text into a small predefined set of labels

requests.title: Four classification routes
requests.show: Four side-by-side pipelines showing task-specific model, frozen embeddings plus classifier, zero-shot label similarity, and generative prompting
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should see that the same classification goal can be solved with very different model architectures and training requirements

requests.title: Task-specific versus embedding classification
requests.show: Show a pretrained task-specific encoder going directly from text to sentiment label beside a frozen embedding encoder producing a vector that then feeds logistic regression
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that the first model performs the task directly while the second separates feature extraction from classification

requests.title: Task-specific sentiment inference
requests.show: Show a movie-review sentence flowing through tokenizer → pretrained sentiment encoder → negative/neutral/positive score outputs, with negative and positive mapped into the chapter's binary labels
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that the model has already learned the classification task and no new training is being performed here

requests.title: Binary confusion matrix
requests.show: A 2×2 matrix labeled TN, FP, FN, TP using negative and positive movie reviews on the axes, with correct cells visually distinguished from error cells
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should be able to identify all four outcomes before learning precision and recall

requests.title: Precision vs recall intuition
requests.show: Show a collection of actual positive items and predicted-positive items as overlapping sets, with TP in the overlap, FP in predicted-only, and FN in actual-only; annotate precision as purity of predictions and recall as coverage of true positives
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should understand the different questions precision and recall answer

requests.title: Frozen embeddings plus logistic regression
requests.show: Show movie reviews entering a frozen embedding model, producing fixed-size vectors, then those vectors and labels feeding a small trainable logistic-regression classifier
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that only the small classifier is trained while the embedding model remains unchanged

requests.title: Zero-shot label embeddings
requests.show: Show a review sentence and two label descriptions (“A negative review”, “A positive review”) each passing through the same embedding model into vectors
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that natural-language labels become comparable vectors without supervised fitting

requests.title: Cosine zero-shot classification
requests.show: Show one document embedding as an arrow and two candidate-label vectors; one label vector has a smaller angle/higher similarity and is selected
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should understand that classification is performed by semantic proximity rather than a separately trained classifier

requests.title: Generative classification versus task-specific classification
requests.show: Show task-specific model: text → numeric class scores, beside generative model: instruction + text → generated class word
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that generative classification requires explicitly expressing the task in the prompt

requests.title: T5 text-to-text unification
requests.show: Show several tasks such as sentiment classification, summarization, and question answering all converted into textual prompts entering the same encoder-decoder model and producing textual outputs
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should see how text-to-text framing unifies tasks

requests.title: Closed-model evaluation caveats
requests.show: Show an API-based classifier with three warning branches: usage cost, rate limits/retries, and unknown training-data overlap with benchmark datasets
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that model quality is only one part of production evaluation

requests.title: Supervised classification versus unsupervised clustering
requests.show: Left side shows labeled documents being assigned to predefined categories; right side shows unlabeled documents automatically forming semantic groups
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that clustering discovers structure rather than learning predefined labels

requests.title: Cluster to topic
requests.show: Show a cluster containing several semantically related documents, then extract representative keywords, then assign a human-readable topic concept
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should understand that clustering groups documents while topic representation helps explain what each group is about

requests.title: Three-step clustering pipeline
requests.show: Show documents → embedding model → high-dimensional vectors → UMAP dimensionality reduction → low-dimensional vectors → HDBSCAN → clusters/outliers
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should memorize the order and role of the three stages

requests.title: Document embedding space
requests.show: Show several short document snippets becoming dense vectors and then points in a conceptual semantic space where similar topics lie near one another
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that clustering works on vectors, not raw strings

requests.title: High-dimensional to low-dimensional representation
requests.show: Show a cloud of conceptual high-dimensional document vectors being compressed into a lower-dimensional space while trying to keep neighboring groups together
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should see dimensionality reduction as structure-preserving compression rather than dropping random features

requests.title: Centroid clustering versus density clustering
requests.show: Show k-means forcing all points into a fixed number of centroid-centered groups beside HDBSCAN discovering dense irregular groups and leaving isolated points as outliers
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should understand why density clustering is attractive when the number of clusters is unknown

requests.title: Cluster visualization with outliers
requests.show: A 2D scatter plot concept showing several colored document clusters and gray outliers, with a warning callout that 2D positions are an approximation of the original high-dimensional embedding space
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should use plots for exploration, not as proof of semantic structure

requests.title: BERTopic two-stage pipeline
requests.show: First stage shows embedding → UMAP → HDBSCAN clustering; second stage shows cluster documents combined and processed with c-TF-IDF to generate ranked topic keywords
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should remember semantic grouping and topic representation as related but separable stages

requests.title: Document TF to class-level TF
requests.show: Show several documents inside one cluster being merged conceptually into one class-level text, then count words over the whole cluster
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that BERTopic represents topics at cluster level rather than treating each document independently

requests.title: c-TF-IDF intuition
requests.show: Show two clusters with word-frequency bars: common stop words are frequent in both and receive low discriminative weight, while a topic-specific word such as “translation” is frequent in one cluster and receives high weight
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should understand why frequency alone is not enough

requests.title: BERTopic as Lego blocks
requests.show: Show interchangeable blocks for embedding, reduction, clustering, and topic representation, with example alternatives underneath each block
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that components can be swapped independently

requests.title: Topic representation refinement
requests.show: Show documents already clustered, c-TF-IDF producing candidate topic keywords, and an additional representation block reranking/refining those keywords without reclustering documents
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should see why topic-level refinement can be much cheaper than document-level processing

requests.title: MMR keyword diversification
requests.show: Show a redundant candidate list with several near-duplicate words being filtered into a smaller list containing relevant but more diverse concepts
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that MMR trades some redundancy for broader topic coverage

requests.title: Generative topic labeling
requests.show: Show one topic cluster producing a small set of representative documents plus top keywords, these entering a generative model once, and a concise human-readable topic label emerging
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should understand why generative labeling is applied per topic instead of per document

requests.title: Complete text clustering and topic modeling pipeline
requests.show: Show unlabeled documents → embedding model → UMAP → HDBSCAN → clusters/outliers → c-TF-IDF → topic keywords → optional KeyBERT/MMR/generative representation blocks → human-readable topics and visualizations
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should be able to use this figure as the final mental model for the chapter

requests.title: Prompt engineering feedback loop
requests.show: Show task requirements → draft prompt → LLM output → evaluate output → revise prompt → repeat
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that prompt engineering is an optimization loop rather than a one-time wording exercise

requests.title: Chat template transformation
requests.show: Show a Python messages list with user/assistant roles on the left and the model-specific serialized prompt with special role and end tokens on the right
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that the chat API/pipeline transforms conversational messages into a model-specific token sequence

requests.title: Deterministic versus sampled next-token selection
requests.show: Show one probability distribution over candidate next tokens; left path always selects the highest candidate, right path samples among candidates according to adjusted probabilities
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should distinguish model probabilities from the decoding policy that chooses the actual output token

requests.title: Temperature comparison
requests.show: Show the same candidate-token distribution at low and high temperature, with low temperature sharply concentrated on top choices and high temperature flatter across more alternatives
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should understand temperature as reshaping the distribution rather than directly adding random words

requests.title: top-p versus top-k
requests.show: Show one ranked token probability list; highlight a cumulative-probability nucleus for top-p and exactly the top K entries for top-k
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should understand that top-p uses probability mass while top-k uses a fixed candidate count

requests.title: Prompt anatomy basics
requests.show: Show a prompt divided into three labeled blocks—Instruction, Data, and Output Indicator—with arrows showing how each constrains the model response
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should see that a prompt can be designed from modular components

requests.title: Modular prompt components
requests.show: Show a prompt assembled from separate labeled blocks: Persona, Instruction, Context, Format, Audience, Tone, and Data
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should see prompt design as composable rather than as one unstructured paragraph

requests.title: Zero-shot one-shot few-shot
requests.show: Three prompt diagrams: instruction only, instruction plus one demonstration, and instruction plus several demonstrations
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should understand that the difference is the number of examples supplied in the current context

requests.title: Prompt chaining pipeline
requests.show: Show product features entering Prompt 1 to generate name/slogan, then those outputs plus original features entering Prompt 2 to generate a sales pitch
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should see how intermediate outputs become inputs to later stages

requests.title: Reasoning-oriented prompt structure
requests.show: Show problem → intermediate substeps/calculations → final answer, with a note that the visible explanation is generated output rather than a guaranteed view of hidden internal computation
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should understand the purpose of structured intermediate reasoning without confusing it with model internals

requests.title: Self-consistency voting
requests.show: Show one prompt branching into several independently sampled reasoning/output paths and then a majority-vote or aggregation node
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should see how repeated sampling trades additional compute for robustness

requests.title: Tree-style solution exploration
requests.show: Show one problem branching into several candidate intermediate ideas, each evaluated, weak branches pruned, and promising branches expanded toward a final answer
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should see the contrast between one linear solution path and deliberate branch exploration

requests.title: Generation plus validation architecture
requests.show: Show LLM generation flowing through separate checks for schema, allowed values, safety/policy, and factual/task validation before output is accepted
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should understand that production reliability requires layers beyond prompting

requests.title: Normal sampling versus constrained sampling
requests.show: Left side shows a wide set of possible next tokens including invalid outputs; right side shows a grammar filter removing illegal candidates so only schema-valid tokens can be selected
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should understand that constraints act during decoding rather than merely asking the model politely

requests.lesson_title: Advanced Text Generation Techniques and Tools
requests.title: LLM system building blocks
requests.show: Show an LLM in the center connected to model I/O, prompt templates/chains, memory, tools, and agent logic
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that the language model is one component inside a larger application architecture

requests.lesson_title: Advanced Text Generation Techniques and Tools
requests.title: Modular LLM framework
requests.show: Show independent blocks labeled Model, Prompt, Memory, Tool, Chain, Agent connected through arrows, with a note that frameworks orchestrate these components
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should see the framework as glue/orchestration rather than the intelligence itself

requests.lesson_title: Advanced Text Generation Techniques and Tools
requests.title: Quantization intuition
requests.show: Show the same numerical value represented with high precision and reduced precision, followed by a large model shrinking in memory footprint
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should understand quantization as reduced parameter precision rather than deleting entire model layers

requests.lesson_title: Advanced Text Generation Techniques and Tools
requests.title: Basic chain
requests.show: Show user variable → prompt template → formatted model prompt → LLM → response
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should see that a chain turns repeated formatting logic into a reusable workflow

requests.lesson_title: Advanced Text Generation Techniques and Tools
requests.title: Sequential story chain
requests.show: Show input summary flowing into title generation, then summary + title into character generation, then all previous outputs into story generation
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that intermediate outputs become named inputs to later stages

requests.lesson_title: Advanced Text Generation Techniques and Tools
requests.title: Stateless calls versus memory-backed conversation
requests.show: Left side shows two independent calls where the second cannot see the first; right side shows conversation history appended to the second call so the model can use earlier information
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should understand that application memory works by re-supplying relevant prior information

requests.lesson_title: Advanced Text Generation Techniques and Tools
requests.title: Full conversation buffer
requests.show: Show an expanding chat history block copied into every new prompt before the latest user message
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should see that memory is achieved by repeatedly sending old text back to the model

requests.lesson_title: Advanced Text Generation Techniques and Tools
requests.title: Windowed conversation memory
requests.show: Show a long conversation timeline where only the latest two interaction blocks are highlighted and inserted into the next prompt while older blocks are discarded
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should understand how a fixed memory window trades history coverage for bounded prompt size

requests.lesson_title: Advanced Text Generation Techniques and Tools
requests.title: Conversation summary memory
requests.show: Show raw chat turns going into a summarizer LLM, producing a compact running summary that is inserted into the main assistant prompt
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should see summary memory as compression rather than simple deletion

requests.lesson_title: Advanced Text Generation Techniques and Tools
requests.title: Chain versus agent
requests.show: Left side shows a fixed predefined chain of steps; right side shows an agent choosing among several tools/actions based on the current task
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should understand fixed orchestration versus dynamic action selection

requests.lesson_title: Advanced Text Generation Techniques and Tools
requests.title: LLM tool use
requests.show: Show an agent receiving a user question and selecting among a web search tool, calculator, and direct answer path, then receiving tool results back
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should see tools as external capabilities selected by orchestration logic

requests.lesson_title: Advanced Text Generation Techniques and Tools
requests.title: ReAct-style loop
requests.show: Show Question → Plan/Thought → Action → Tool → Observation → back to Plan/Thought, eventually ending in Final Answer
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should understand how tool results become new context for subsequent decisions

requests.lesson_title: Advanced Text Generation Techniques and Tools
requests.title: Agent reliability controls
requests.show: Show an agent/tool loop surrounded by controls for tool permissions, source capture, validation, logging, human review, and error handling
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should understand that autonomy must be paired with guardrails and observability

requests.lesson_title: Advanced Text Generation Techniques and Tools
requests.title: Complete memory-agent-tool system
requests.show: Show user request entering an agent with access to memory, search, calculator, and validation; observations flow back to the agent before a final response
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should see how the chapter’s separate components combine into one application

requests.title: Keyword search versus semantic search
requests.show: Show the same query entering two pipelines: keyword search matching shared words and semantic search matching a differently worded but meaning-equivalent passage
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that semantic relevance does not require exact query terms

requests.title: Basic RAG motivation
requests.show: Show a question going first to search, retrieved evidence entering the LLM together with the question, and the LLM producing an answer with source references
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should understand that retrieval supplies evidence before generation

requests.title: Retrieval reranking RAG stack
requests.show: Show a three-stage pipeline with dense/lexical retrieval producing candidates, reranker reordering them, and a generative model answering from the top evidence
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should see retrieval, reranking, and generation as distinct jobs

requests.title: Dense retrieval embedding space
requests.show: Show query and several document points in a vector space, with the nearest two documents highlighted as retrieved results
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should connect semantic similarity with nearest-neighbor retrieval

requests.title: Vector indexing and retrieval
requests.show: Two phases: indexing phase with documents → chunks → embeddings → vector index, and query phase with query → embedding → nearest-neighbor lookup → retrieved chunks
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should distinguish offline indexing from online query retrieval

requests.title: BM25 versus dense retrieval example
requests.show: Show the same query with BM25 selecting a passage that shares the word “science,” while dense retrieval selects a passage about “scientific accuracy”
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should understand lexical overlap versus semantic relevance

requests.title: Hybrid search architecture
requests.show: Show one query branching to BM25 and dense retrieval, candidate lists being merged, then sent to reranking
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should see hybrid search as combining complementary retrieval signals

requests.title: Whole document vector versus chunk vectors
requests.show: Show one long document mapped to a single compressed vector on the left, and the same document split into multiple topic-specific chunks with separate vectors on the right
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should see why multiple chunk vectors preserve more retrievable detail

requests.title: Chunking strategies
requests.show: Show one document split four ways: sentence chunks, paragraph chunks, fixed multi-sentence chunks, and overlapping chunks with shared boundary text
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should understand that chunk size and overlap change retrieval behavior

requests.title: Retrieval fine-tuning positive and negative pairs
requests.show: Show one relevant document with two positive query arrows being pulled closer and one irrelevant query arrow being pushed farther away after training
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should understand retrieval fine-tuning as shaping the geometry around task-specific relevance

requests.title: Two-stage retrieval and reranking
requests.show: Show a huge corpus narrowed by a fast first-stage retriever to a small candidate set, followed by a slower relevance reranker producing the final ordered results
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should understand why reranking is normally applied to a shortlist rather than the whole corpus

requests.title: Bi-encoder versus cross-encoder
requests.show: Left side shows query and document encoded independently then compared; right side shows query and document entering the same model together to produce one relevance score
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should understand why cross-encoders can judge relevance more deeply but are more expensive

requests.title: Retrieval evaluation test set
requests.show: Show a query linked to a corpus with certain documents marked relevant, then a search system returning a ranked list that can be scored against those relevance judgments
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should see that search evaluation requires labeled relevance data

requests.title: Average Precision calculation
requests.show: Show a ranked list with relevant items highlighted at positions 1 and 3, annotate precision@1 and precision@3, then average them
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should understand that AP rewards earlier relevant documents

requests.title: Basic RAG pipeline
requests.show: Show question → retriever → top evidence chunks → prompt containing question + context → LLM → grounded answer with citations
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should memorize retrieval first, generation second

requests.title: Local RAG components
requests.show: Show documents indexed by an embedding model into a local FAISS vector store, with question → retriever → context → prompt → local LLM → answer
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should see that RAG can be implemented entirely from modular local components

requests.title: Query rewriting
requests.show: Show a long conversational user message being condensed by an LLM into a short search-optimized query before retrieval
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should understand that user language and retrieval language can differ

requests.title: Multi-hop RAG
requests.show: Show first retrieval producing entities, then each entity generating follow-up queries whose evidence is combined into a final answer
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should see that later retrieval depends on earlier retrieval results

requests.title: Agentic RAG architecture
requests.show: Show an LLM/controller choosing among several retrieval tools/data sources, inspecting observations, issuing follow-up queries, then generating a final grounded answer
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should connect advanced RAG with the agent/tool ideas from Chapter 7

requests.title: RAG evaluation dimensions
requests.show: Show a RAG answer surrounded by evaluation checks for retrieval quality, faithfulness, answer relevance, citation precision/recall, fluency, and utility
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should see that RAG quality is multidimensional

requests.title: Complete semantic search and RAG architecture
requests.show: Show offline indexing with chunking/embeddings/vector database and online flow with query rewrite → hybrid retrieval → reranker → context assembly → generator → cited answer, with evaluation attached to both retrieval and generation
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should use this as the final architecture map for the chapter

requests.title: Multimodal model overview
requests.show: Show several modalities—text, image, audio, video, sensors—feeding a multimodal model, with text as one possible output
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that input modality support and output modality support are separate capabilities

requests.title: Text Transformer versus Vision Transformer
requests.show: Left side shows text → tokens → embeddings → Transformer encoder; right side shows image → patches → patch embeddings → Transformer encoder
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should see that tokenization and patching play analogous preprocessing roles

requests.title: Image patching
requests.show: Show a single image divided into a regular grid of patches, then the patches flattened into a sequence P1, P2, P3, ...
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should understand image patching as the visual analogue of converting a sentence into a token sequence

requests.title: Patch embedding pipeline
requests.show: Show image patch → flattened pixel vector → linear projection → dense patch embedding, repeated for several patches before entering a Transformer encoder
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should understand how raw visual data is turned into Transformer-compatible numerical representations

requests.title: Shared image-text embedding space
requests.show: Show image embeddings and text embeddings as points in the same vector space, with matching image-caption pairs close together and unrelated pairs farther apart
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should understand why shared embedding geometry enables cross-modal comparison

requests.title: CLIP dual encoder
requests.show: Show a text encoder and an image encoder processing a caption and its matching image separately, producing two embeddings in the same vector space
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should see CLIP as a dual-encoder alignment model

requests.title: CLIP contrastive training matrix
requests.show: Show a batch of images on one axis and captions on the other, forming a similarity matrix where diagonal matching pairs are highlighted as positives and off-diagonal pairs are negatives
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should understand why batch-wise contrastive learning provides both positive and negative examples

requests.title: CLIP applications
requests.show: Show a shared embedding space branching into zero-shot classification, image search from text, text search from image, clustering, and generation conditioning
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should understand that one aligned representation space enables many applications

requests.title: Image preprocessing tensor shape
requests.show: Show a normal RGB image being resized/normalized into a tensor labeled [batch=1, channels=3, height=224, width=224]
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should be able to interpret the four tensor dimensions

requests.title: BLIP-2 high-level architecture
requests.show: Show frozen Vision Transformer → trainable Q-Former → projection → frozen LLM, clearly marking which components are frozen and which bridge is trainable
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should understand BLIP-2 as connecting pretrained models instead of retraining everything

requests.title: BLIP-2 stage 1 objectives
requests.show: Show image and caption inputs entering Q-Former training with three output branches labeled contrastive alignment, image-text matching, and image-grounded text generation
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should remember the three complementary objectives

requests.title: Soft visual prompt bridge
requests.show: Show Q-Former visual outputs passing through a linear projection into a sequence of LLM-compatible embedding vectors inserted before textual prompt embeddings
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should understand how image information becomes conditioning context for the LLM

requests.title: Aspect-ratio preprocessing caution
requests.show: Show a wide original image being transformed into a square 224×224 model input, with visual distortion highlighted
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should recognize that preprocessing itself can alter visual information

requests.title: Image captioning pipeline
requests.show: Show an image entering processor → vision encoder/Q-Former → LLM → generated caption
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should understand captioning as visual input conditioned text generation

requests.title: Visual question answering
requests.show: Show an image and textual question entering the multimodal model together, producing a text answer tied to visual evidence
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should distinguish VQA from unconditional image captioning

requests.title: Multimodal chat memory
requests.show: Show one persistent image plus conversation history—Q1/A1, Q2/A2—being assembled into the next multimodal prompt
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should connect multimodal chat with application-managed conversation memory

requests.title: CLIP versus BLIP-2
requests.show: Side-by-side diagram: CLIP maps image/text to shared embeddings for similarity, while BLIP-2 maps image features through Q-Former/projection into an LLM for text generation
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should clearly distinguish multimodal retrieval embeddings from multimodal generation

requests.title: Complete multimodal architecture map
requests.show: Show three stacked stages: ViT patch representation, CLIP shared image-text embedding alignment, and BLIP-2 visual-to-language generation bridge
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should use this figure as the chapter’s final mental map

requests.title: Text to embedding
requests.show: Show a document, sentence, and phrase entering an embedding model and each becoming a dense numerical vector
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should understand embeddings as learned numerical representations rather than arbitrary encodings

requests.title: Semantic space versus sentiment space
requests.show: Show the same documents organized in two embedding spaces: one grouping by semantic topic and another grouping by positive/negative sentiment
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should see that fine-tuning changes what “similarity” means

requests.title: Contrastive learning geometry
requests.show: Show an anchor sentence, a positive sentence being pulled closer in vector space, and a negative sentence being pushed farther away
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should understand contrastive learning as reshaping embedding geometry through comparisons

requests.title: Cross-encoder architecture
requests.show: Show sentence A and sentence B concatenated with a separator and passed through one Transformer that produces a similarity score
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that the pair must be processed together for every comparison

requests.title: Bi-encoder versus cross-encoder
requests.show: Left side shows cross-encoder processing a pair together for one score; right side shows the same shared encoder independently generating reusable embeddings that can later be compared
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should understand why bi-encoders scale better for retrieval

requests.title: NLI as contrastive data
requests.show: Show one premise with an entailment hypothesis, neutral hypothesis, and contradiction hypothesis branching from it
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should understand how NLI labels naturally create different similarity relationships

requests.title: STSB evaluation
requests.show: Show human-labeled sentence similarity scores compared with cosine similarity produced from model embeddings, then compute a correlation metric
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should understand that evaluation checks whether embedding geometry agrees with human similarity judgments

requests.title: Multi-task embedding evaluation
requests.show: Show one embedding model evaluated across several task families such as similarity, classification, clustering, and retrieval
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should understand why broad evaluation is more informative than one benchmark score

requests.title: Cosine similarity loss
requests.show: Show two sentence embeddings with a target similarity score; training adjusts their angle so predicted cosine similarity approaches the labeled value
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should understand cosine loss as matching vector similarity to human/data-provided similarity

requests.title: Multiple Negatives Ranking loss
requests.show: Show one anchor compared against one positive and several in-batch negative candidates, with the positive required to receive the highest similarity
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should see MNR as a ranking problem within a batch

requests.title: Easy versus semi-hard versus hard negatives
requests.show: Show an anchor query with three negative answers: unrelated, topically related, and highly similar but incorrect
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should understand that difficult negatives force the model to learn finer semantic distinctions

requests.title: Augmented SBERT overview
requests.show: Show small gold dataset → train cross-encoder teacher → label many unlabeled sentence pairs → silver dataset → combine gold + silver → train bi-encoder/SBERT
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should memorize the teacher-labeler-student workflow

requests.title: TSDAE denoising autoencoder
requests.show: Show original sentence → word deletion/noise → damaged sentence → encoder → single sentence embedding → decoder → reconstructed original sentence
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should understand that reconstruction pressure teaches the embedding to preserve sentence information

requests.title: Domain adaptation
requests.show: Show a generic source-domain embedding model being adapted using unlabeled target-domain documents, producing a new model whose representation space better reflects target terminology and concepts
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should understand domain adaptation as specialization rather than training from nothing

requests.title: Embedding model development lifecycle
requests.show: Show objective definition → data pairs/negatives → model/loss → training → evaluation → error analysis → better data/domain adaptation → retraining
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should see embedding development as an iterative data-and-objective loop

requests.title: Frozen versus fine-tuned classifier
requests.show: Left side shows frozen BERT feeding a trainable classifier; right side shows both BERT and classification head trainable with backward arrows through the whole network
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should see the difference between fixed feature extraction and end-to-end task adaptation

requests.title: Task-specific BERT classifier
requests.show: Show tokenized text entering pretrained BERT, pooled representation entering a small feedforward classification head, and gradients flowing backward through both components
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should understand joint optimization

requests.title: Dynamic batch padding
requests.show: Show three token sequences of different lengths being padded to the length of the longest sequence in that batch
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should understand why padding is required for tensor batches without padding every sample to a global maximum

requests.title: Layer-freezing spectrum
requests.show: Show BERT embeddings + 12 encoder blocks + classifier, with three configurations: all trainable, only classifier trainable, and only later encoder blocks plus classifier trainable
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should understand freezing as a continuum rather than an all-or-nothing choice

requests.title: Partial BERT freezing
requests.show: Show early encoder blocks locked and later encoder blocks plus classifier unlocked, with gradient flow only through the trainable tail
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should see why partial fine-tuning can preserve adaptability while reducing compute

requests.title: Few-shot classification
requests.show: Show two classes with only a small handful of labeled examples feeding a model that must classify unseen text
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should understand the low-label-data setting

requests.title: Three-stage SetFit pipeline
requests.show: Show class-labeled examples → positive/negative pair generation → contrastive SentenceTransformer fine-tuning → embeddings → classifier
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should memorize the three SetFit stages

requests.title: Two-stage versus three-stage adaptation
requests.show: Show standard pretrained model → task fine-tuning beside pretrained model → continued domain MLM → task fine-tuning
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should see where domain adaptation fits

requests.title: Token masking versus whole-word masking
requests.show: Show one tokenized sentence where a single subword is masked versus another where all subwords belonging to one word are masked
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should understand why whole-word masking is a harder prediction task

requests.title: MLM before versus after domain adaptation
requests.show: Show the same masked sentence with general BERT predicting generic nouns and movie-domain-adapted BERT predicting film-related nouns
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should see evidence that continued pretraining shifts the model toward domain language

requests.title: Document classification versus NER
requests.show: Left side shows one review receiving one sentiment label; right side shows one sentence with entity labels attached to individual token spans
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should see the shift from sequence-level to token-level prediction

requests.title: BIO entity span
requests.show: Show “Dean Palmer” with Dean labeled B-PER and Palmer labeled I-PER, plus “Rangers” labeled B-ORG and non-entities labeled O
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should understand how BIO tags preserve phrase boundaries

requests.title: Word-to-subword label mismatch
requests.show: Show one labeled word such as “Maarten/B-PER” split into Ma, ##arte, ##n, creating multiple token positions that need aligned labels
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should see why token classification requires special preprocessing

requests.title: NER subtoken inference
requests.show: Show “Maarten” tokenized into Ma / ##arte / ##n with B-PER / I-PER / I-PER, then reconstructed visually as one person entity span
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should connect subtoken predictions back to a human-readable entity

requests.title: Chapter 11 adaptation map
requests.show: Show five branches from a pretrained representation model: full sequence fine-tuning, partial freezing, SetFit, continued MLM then classification, and token-level NER
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should use this as the final decision map for the chapter

requests.title: Three-stage LLM training pipeline
requests.show: Show an untrained Transformer progressing through pretraining → base model, supervised fine-tuning → instruction/chat model, and preference tuning → aligned model
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should memorize the different purpose of each stage

requests.title: Base model continuation versus instruction model
requests.show: Show the same user question sent to a base model that continues with more questions and an instruction-tuned model that answers directly
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should understand why instruction following is a separate learned behavior

requests.title: SFT training example
requests.show: Show user instruction + desired assistant response converted into a training sequence where the model learns to predict the response tokens conditioned on the user message
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should see that SFT still uses token prediction but on curated instruction data

requests.title: Full fine-tuning versus PEFT
requests.show: Show a full model with every block highlighted as trainable beside a mostly frozen model with only small adapter/LoRA components highlighted
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should understand PEFT as reducing the trainable parameter set

requests.title: Swappable adapters
requests.show: Show one shared frozen Transformer backbone with several small adapter sets that can be swapped for medical, NER, and legal tasks
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should understand the storage and modularity benefit

requests.title: LoRA matrix update
requests.show: Show large frozen matrix W plus a low-rank update ΔW formed by multiplying two narrow matrices A and B, producing effective weight W + ΔW
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should understand that LoRA learns a compact weight change rather than replacing the full matrix

requests.title: Numerical precision and memory
requests.show: Show one weight represented in 32-bit, 16-bit, 8-bit, and 4-bit forms with decreasing memory use and increasing approximation
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should understand the core quantization tradeoff

requests.title: QLoRA architecture
requests.show: Show frozen 4-bit base model weights with small trainable LoRA matrices attached to selected projection layers
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should understand why QLoRA can fine-tune models that would otherwise exceed available VRAM

requests.title: Instruction-tuning chat template
requests.show: Show raw conversation messages being serialized into model-specific user/assistant tokens and end-of-message markers
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should connect chat templates from Chapter 6 with SFT training data

requests.title: Gradient accumulation
requests.show: Show four small mini-batches processed sequentially, gradients accumulated, then one optimizer update
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should understand how small-memory training can emulate a larger batch size

requests.title: LoRA adapter merge
requests.show: Show frozen base model and separate LoRA adapter being combined into one merged model for inference
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should understand adapter-only storage versus merged deployment

requests.title: Perplexity intuition
requests.show: Show a phrase ending before the next token, with one model assigning high probability to the correct continuation and another distributing probability poorly
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should understand perplexity as next-token predictive confidence

requests.title: LLM-as-a-judge pairwise evaluation
requests.show: Show two candidate model responses to one prompt being compared by a separate judge model that returns a preference
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should understand automated qualitative comparison

requests.title: Goodhart's Law in LLM evaluation
requests.show: Show a model optimizing one metric upward while broader usefulness drops, illustrating benchmark gaming/over-optimization
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should understand why evaluation needs multiple independent perspectives

requests.title: Reward model
requests.show: Show prompt + generated response entering a reward model derived from an instruction-tuned model, with the language-modeling head replaced by a scalar scoring head
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should understand how generative output can be converted into a trainable preference score

requests.title: Preference data collection
requests.show: Show one prompt sent to the same model twice to create response A and B, then a human chooses one as preferred
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should see how pairwise feedback becomes training data

requests.title: Reward-model-based RLHF pipeline
requests.show: Show preference collection → reward model training → policy/LLM optimization with reward feedback
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should understand the full alignment loop

requests.title: DPO versus reward-model RLHF
requests.show: Left side shows preference data → reward model → PPO → LLM; right side shows preference data directly comparing frozen reference and trainable model probabilities
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should see why DPO removes the explicit reward-model training stage

requests.title: SFT then DPO
requests.show: Show a base model first receiving instruction tuning and then preference tuning, with each stage labeled by the type of data it uses
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should understand why instruction following and preference alignment are separate capabilities

requests.title: Complete generative fine-tuning lifecycle
requests.show: Show pretraining → base LLM → SFT with LoRA/QLoRA option → instruction model → evaluation → reward-model/PPO or DPO preference tuning → aligned model → deployment evaluation
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should use this as the final mental map for Chapter 12

requests.lesson_title: Building AI Applications with Foundation Models
requests.title: From traditional ML to AI engineering
requests.show: A two-lane diagram comparing the traditional workflow of collecting data and training a task-specific model with the foundation-model workflow of selecting an existing model, adapting it, evaluating it, and integrating it into an application
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that AI engineering shifts much of the effort from model creation toward model adaptation and product development

requests.lesson_title: Building AI Applications with Foundation Models
requests.title: Tokenization example
requests.show: A short English sentence visually split into several word and subword tokens, including at least one word divided into two tokens
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that tokens are not always identical to words and that tokenization controls the units the model processes

requests.lesson_title: Building AI Applications with Foundation Models
requests.title: Masked versus autoregressive language models
requests.show: A side-by-side diagram where the masked model fills a blank using context on both sides and the autoregressive model predicts the next token using only preceding tokens
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice the different information available to each model during prediction

requests.lesson_title: Building AI Applications with Foundation Models
requests.title: Multimodal foundation model
requests.show: A diagram with text tokens and image tokens entering the same model and a generated output token leaving it
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that the model can condition its output on multiple modalities rather than text alone

requests.lesson_title: Building AI Applications with Foundation Models
requests.title: Foundation-model use-case map
requests.show: A compact map or wheel showing coding, visual generation, writing, education, conversational bots, information aggregation, data organization, and workflow automation around a central foundation model
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that one general-purpose model can support many application categories

requests.lesson_title: Building AI Applications with Foundation Models
requests.title: Crawl-Walk-Run automation maturity
requests.show: A three-stage diagram showing mandatory human review, internal direct AI use, and higher automation with possible external-user interaction
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that automation can increase gradually as confidence and evidence improve

requests.lesson_title: Building AI Applications with Foundation Models
requests.title: Three-layer AI engineering stack
requests.show: A vertical stack with Application Development on top, Model Development in the middle, and Infrastructure at the bottom, with two or three example responsibilities inside each layer
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that most application builders can begin at the top and move down only when more control is necessary

requests.lesson_title: Building AI Applications with Foundation Models
requests.title: Product-first AI engineering workflow
requests.show: A simple loop showing idea -> existing foundation model -> product prototype -> user feedback -> evaluation -> better data/model adaptation -> improved product
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that modern AI teams can validate the product earlier instead of waiting for a custom model to be trained first

requests.title: Foundation-model design map
requests.show: A four-part diagram showing training data, architecture/scale, post-training, and sampling all feeding into downstream model behavior
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that application behavior is influenced by choices made both during training and during inference

requests.title: Uneven multilingual representation
requests.show: A simple bar chart contrasting one highly represented language with several low-resource languages in a web-scale dataset
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that model exposure to languages can differ dramatically and that this can influence downstream performance

requests.title: Seq2seq versus transformer
requests.show: A side-by-side diagram showing an RNN encoder-decoder compressing input into a sequential representation versus a transformer where output generation can attend directly to relevant previous tokens
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that attention gives the model richer access to earlier information and that transformer input processing is more parallelizable

requests.title: Query-Key-Value attention
requests.show: A simplified attention diagram with one query comparing against several keys, producing attention weights that determine how strongly the corresponding values contribute to the result
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice the difference between deciding relevance with Q/K and retrieving information through V

requests.title: Simplified transformer architecture
requests.show: A vertical diagram showing token/position embeddings, repeated transformer blocks containing attention and MLP modules, then an output layer producing token scores
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that a transformer is a stack of repeated blocks rather than a single attention operation

requests.title: Dense model versus mixture of experts
requests.show: A simple diagram where every block is active in a dense model, while a router sends each token to only a small subset of expert blocks in an MoE model
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice the difference between total and active parameters

requests.title: Pre-training to post-training pipeline
requests.show: A three-stage diagram showing self-supervised pre-training, supervised finetuning, and preference finetuning
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that conversational behavior is shaped after the base model has already learned broad capabilities

requests.title: Logits to sampled token
requests.show: A pipeline showing a vector of raw logits, softmax converting them to probabilities, and one token being selected according to a sampling strategy
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that the model first scores all candidate tokens and sampling happens only after those scores are produced

requests.title: Top-k versus top-p
requests.show: A token-probability bar chart showing top-k selecting a fixed number of highest tokens while top-p selects however many tokens are needed to reach a cumulative probability threshold
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that top-k fixes the count while top-p adapts the count to the distribution

requests.title: Constrained sampling for structured output
requests.show: A diagram showing raw logits over many tokens being filtered by a grammar so that only tokens valid for the target structure remain before sampling
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that invalid tokens can be prevented during generation instead of repaired afterward

requests.title: Snowballing hallucination
requests.show: A causal chain showing an initial incorrect generated assumption followed by several later tokens/statements that become increasingly wrong because they are conditioned on the first mistake
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice how an early error can compound during autoregressive generation

requests.title: Evaluation around failure modes
requests.show: A diagram showing an AI application in the center, surrounded by possible failure areas such as factual errors, unsafe outputs, poor retrieval, tool failure, latency, and user dissatisfaction, with evaluation methods mapped to those risks
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that evaluation should be designed from concrete failure modes rather than generic scores

requests.title: Entropy and cross entropy intuition
requests.show: A visual with two probability distributions: a predictable two-choice distribution and a less predictable multi-choice distribution, plus a second panel showing a model distribution approximating a true data distribution
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that entropy belongs to the data distribution while cross entropy also reflects model mismatch

requests.title: Functional correctness evaluation
requests.show: A flow diagram showing an AI-generated solution being executed or applied to several test cases, producing pass/fail results
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that the system is judged by behavior rather than textual resemblance

requests.title: Semantic embedding space
requests.show: A 2D conceptual embedding plot where semantically related sentences cluster together even when their wording differs, while unrelated sentences appear far apart
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that semantic similarity operates on meaning rather than word overlap

requests.title: AI judge system
requests.show: A diagram showing generated answer plus evaluation prompt entering a judge model, which returns a score and explanation, with model version, prompt version, and sampling settings labeled as parts of the judge
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that the judge is more than the underlying model name

requests.title: Pairwise comparison graph
requests.show: Several model nodes connected by pairwise matches with win rates, followed by a rating algorithm producing a ranked list
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that ranking is inferred from a network of comparisons rather than one absolute score per model

requests.title: Evaluation-driven development loop
requests.show: A loop showing define criteria -> build prototype -> evaluate -> improve -> deploy -> collect production evidence -> refine criteria
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that evaluation starts before implementation and continues throughout the application's lifecycle

requests.title: Local versus global factual consistency
