requests.show: A split diagram where local factuality compares an answer directly against provided context, while global factuality first retrieves trusted external evidence and then verifies the answer
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that global verification adds an evidence-discovery problem

requests.title: Search-augmented factuality evaluator
requests.show: A four-stage pipeline showing response decomposition, self-contained claims, web or knowledge search, and claim verification
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that long-form factuality can be reduced to verifying smaller atomic claims

requests.title: Quality-cost-latency tradeoff
requests.show: A three-axis conceptual diagram or Pareto frontier where some models are higher quality but slower/more expensive and others are cheaper/faster with lower quality
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that model selection is a multi-objective problem

requests.title: Model-selection funnel
requests.show: A four-stage funnel from all models -> hard-attribute filtering -> public benchmark shortlist -> private evaluation -> production monitoring
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that public benchmarks narrow candidates but do not make the final choice

requests.title: API versus self-hosted decision matrix
requests.show: A two-column matrix comparing external APIs and self-hosted models across privacy, performance, functionality, cost, control, finetuning, and on-device deployment
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that neither option is universally better; the right choice depends on application constraints

requests.title: Public versus private leaderboard
requests.show: A diagram showing public benchmarks feeding a coarse shortlist, then application-specific benchmarks, weights, cost, and latency producing a private model ranking
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that public rankings are only an early filter

requests.title: Component, turn, and task evaluation
requests.show: A layered diagram showing intermediate component metrics at the bottom, turn-level quality in the middle, and end-to-end task success at the top
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that a reliable pipeline measures both local failures and the final user outcome

requests.title: Simpson's paradox in model evaluation
requests.show: A two-group table where Model A performs better than Model B inside each subgroup but Model B has a higher aggregated score due to different group sizes
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice why aggregate metrics must be inspected alongside slice-level results

requests.title: Instructions versus query-specific context
requests.show: A diagram showing a shared system instruction combined with query-specific retrieved/tool-generated context before entering the model
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that instructions stay relatively stable while context changes for each query

requests.title: Basic RAG architecture
requests.show: A simple pipeline showing query -> retriever -> external memory -> retrieved chunks -> prompt construction -> generator -> answer
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice the two core components: retriever and generator

requests.title: TF-IDF and inverted index intuition
requests.show: A small corpus with an inverted index mapping rare and common query terms to documents, plus relevance scores
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that frequent terms inside one document help, but terms common across every document carry less weight

requests.title: Semantic retrieval pipeline
requests.show: A diagram showing documents embedded and stored in a vector database, then a query embedded by the same model and matched to nearby vectors
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that indexing and querying must use compatible embeddings

requests.title: Exact k-NN versus ANN
requests.show: A side-by-side diagram where exact search compares against every vector while ANN navigates only a small graph/cluster subset
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice the accuracy-versus-speed tradeoff

requests.title: Hybrid retrieval with RRF
requests.show: BM25 and vector search running in parallel, producing two ranked lists that are fused into one final ranking before reranking/generation
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice how lexical and semantic evidence complement each other

requests.title: Chunk size and overlap tradeoff
requests.show: One document shown first as large chunks and then as smaller overlapping chunks
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice how overlap protects boundary information while smaller chunks increase index volume

requests.title: Contextual retrieval
requests.show: A document split into chunks, each chunk receiving a short title/summary/entity context before being embedded and indexed
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that the added context makes isolated chunks easier to retrieve correctly

requests.title: Tabular RAG workflow
requests.show: A pipeline showing user question -> relevant schema selection -> text-to-SQL -> database execution -> result -> response generation
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that structured data retrieval often requires tool execution rather than nearest-neighbor document search

requests.title: Agent loop
requests.show: A loop showing user goal -> planner -> tool/action -> environment -> observation -> planner, repeating until completion
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that the model receives feedback from the environment rather than producing one isolated answer

requests.title: Decoupled planning and execution
requests.show: A loop showing plan generation -> plan validation -> execution -> outcome evaluation -> replan, with invalid plans returning to the planner before any tool is called
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that validation can prevent expensive or dangerous execution

requests.title: Agent control-flow patterns
requests.show: Four small diagrams for sequential, parallel, conditional, and loop execution
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that complex agents need more than a simple list of tool calls

requests.title: ReAct and reflection loop
requests.show: A circular diagram showing plan/thought -> action/tool -> observation -> evaluation/reflection -> updated plan
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that observation is fed back into future decisions rather than ignored

requests.title: Three-level AI memory hierarchy
requests.show: A hierarchy showing model weights as internal knowledge, active context as short-term memory, and external persistent stores as long-term memory
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice the tradeoff between persistence, capacity, and access

requests.title: Memory management flow
requests.show: New observation entering a decision node with branches insert, merge, replace, ignore, plus retrieval from long-term memory back into active context
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that useful memory requires active management, not only storage

requests.title: Prompting versus finetuning
requests.show: A side-by-side diagram where prompting changes instructions/context around fixed model weights while finetuning updates some or all model weights
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that the adaptation happens in different places

requests.title: Finetuning family
requests.show: A branching diagram from a pre-trained model to continued pre-training, supervised finetuning, preference finetuning, infilling, and long-context finetuning
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that 'finetuning' is an umbrella for several different training objectives

requests.title: RAG versus finetuning decision tree
requests.show: A decision tree starting with model failure, branching into missing/outdated information toward RAG and behavior/format/style failure toward finetuning, with a later branch allowing both
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that failure diagnosis should drive the adaptation method

requests.title: Forward and backward pass
requests.show: A small neural-network diagram showing forward activations and backward gradients, with loss feeding into parameter updates
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that training stores extra information absent from normal inference

requests.title: Inference versus training memory
requests.show: A stacked bar comparison showing inference memory as weights + activations/KV and training memory adding gradients + optimizer states + larger activation requirements
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice why a model that fits for inference may still not fit for finetuning

requests.title: Quantization memory tradeoff
requests.show: The same model shown at 32-bit, 16-bit, 8-bit, and 4-bit with decreasing memory blocks and a warning that lower precision can introduce numerical error
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice the near-linear memory reduction with bits per value

requests.title: Adapter PEFT versus soft prompts
requests.show: A transformer diagram with one version showing small trainable adapter modules inside the network and another showing trainable soft vectors prepended to model inputs/layers
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that both freeze most base weights but adapt the model at different locations

requests.title: LoRA matrix update
requests.show: A large frozen matrix W beside two small trainable matrices A and B whose product forms a low-rank update added to W
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that only A and B receive gradient updates

requests.title: Multi-LoRA serving
requests.show: One shared base model connected to many small customer/task adapters that are swapped at runtime
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that the expensive base weights are stored once

requests.title: LoRA versus QLoRA
requests.show: Side-by-side diagram where LoRA uses a higher-precision frozen base plus small adapters, while QLoRA stores the frozen base in 4-bit NF4 and trains small adapters with temporary dequantization
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that QLoRA reduces the base-model memory, not merely adapter size

requests.title: Task-vector merging
requests.show: One base model with two finetuned models producing delta/task vectors, then the vectors being combined and added back to the base
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that merging can operate on changes from the shared base rather than raw full weights

requests.title: Layer stacking and upscaling
requests.show: Two copies of a smaller model whose layers are partly stacked and partly combined to create a deeper larger model
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that stacking changes the architecture and normally requires more training

requests.title: Dataset engineering lifecycle
requests.show: A circular workflow showing define behavior -> acquire/annotate -> synthesize -> verify -> inspect/process -> train/evaluate -> return to curation
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that dataset engineering is iterative rather than linear

requests.title: Human versus AI tool workflow
requests.show: A side-by-side flow showing a human using browser UI steps and an AI making direct API/tool calls
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that copying human actions exactly may produce inefficient agent training data

requests.title: Quality coverage quantity triangle
requests.show: A triangle with quality, coverage/diversity, and quantity at the corners, with strong training data in the center
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that increasing only one dimension cannot compensate for failures in the others

requests.title: Dataset-size performance curve
requests.show: A learning curve showing performance rising quickly with early examples and gradually flattening
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice diminishing returns and how the slope informs whether more annotation is worthwhile

requests.title: Synthetic-data motivations
requests.show: Five branches from synthetic data labeled quantity, coverage, quality, privacy, and distillation
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that synthetic data is not only a way to make a dataset bigger

requests.title: Instruction-data synthesis pipeline
requests.show: Seed tasks/topics feeding instruction generation, response generation, verification, filtering, and final SFT dataset
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that generation must be followed by verification and coverage analysis

requests.title: Verified coding-data synthesis
requests.show: Program problem -> generated code -> parser/linter -> unit tests -> correction loop -> verified example, with optional translation/back-translation branches
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that bad generated examples are rejected rather than blindly added to training

requests.title: Synthetic-data feedback loop
requests.show: Real distribution -> model -> synthetic dataset biased toward common cases -> next model -> even narrower distribution, with rare cases fading
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice how repeated synthetic-only training can erase the tails

requests.title: Dataset inspection dashboard
requests.show: Histograms for input length, response length, language, topic, and annotator score alongside a manual-example viewer
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that aggregate statistics and raw-example inspection complement each other

requests.title: Deduplication strategies
requests.show: Three branches showing pairwise similarity, hashing/bucketing, and vector/dimensionality reduction candidate search
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice the tradeoff between exhaustive accuracy and scalable candidate filtering

requests.title: Three levels of inference optimization
requests.show: A layered diagram showing model-level, hardware-level, and service-level optimizations feeding latency and cost outcomes
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that inference efficiency is a systems problem, not only a model problem

requests.title: Roofline model intuition
requests.show: A simplified roofline graph with a bandwidth-limited rising region and compute-limited flat region
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that optimization depends on which side of the bottleneck the workload occupies

requests.title: Prefill versus decode
requests.show: A two-phase LLM inference diagram showing parallel input processing during prefill and one-token-at-a-time generation during decode
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice the different compute profiles

requests.title: TTFT and TPOT timeline
requests.show: A request timeline marking request arrival, first token, subsequent tokens, and completion
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice how first-token delay and per-token generation contribute differently to total latency

requests.title: Throughput versus goodput
requests.show: A bar of all completed requests with only the SLO-satisfying portion highlighted as goodput
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that raw throughput can overstate useful serving capacity

requests.title: Accelerator memory hierarchy
requests.show: A memory pyramid showing CPU DRAM at large/slow bottom, GPU HBM in the middle, and small/fast on-chip SRAM/registers at the top
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice the capacity-versus-bandwidth tradeoff across memory levels

requests.title: Speculative decoding
requests.show: A draft model proposing K tokens and a target model accepting the longest valid prefix in one verification pass
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice how verification parallelizes work that would otherwise be sequential

requests.title: KV-cache reuse
requests.show: Several decoding steps where old K/V vectors remain cached and only the newest token's K/V is added
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that caching removes recomputation but grows memory over the sequence

requests.title: Paged KV cache
requests.show: A comparison between fragmented contiguous KV allocations and page/block-based allocations packed flexibly into GPU memory
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice how paging reduces wasted memory space

requests.title: Operator fusion
requests.show: A before/after diagram where operator A writes an intermediate tensor to memory and operator B reloads it, versus a fused kernel keeping the intermediate on-chip
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice the avoided memory traffic

requests.title: Static versus dynamic batching
requests.show: A timeline of arriving requests where static waits for a full batch and dynamic launches when full or timeout occurs
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice the throughput-versus-queueing-latency tradeoff

requests.title: Continuous batching
requests.show: A batch-slot timeline where one request finishes early and is immediately replaced by a new request while longer requests continue
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice why variable-length workloads benefit from in-flight batching

requests.title: Prompt caching
requests.show: Two requests sharing a long system prompt where the first request computes/caches the prefix and the second reuses it while only processing the new user suffix
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice which computation is avoided

requests.title: Parallelism families
requests.show: A comparison of replica parallelism (full copies), tensor parallelism (split operator tensors), pipeline parallelism (split layers), and context parallelism (split sequence)
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice what dimension each strategy partitions

requests.lesson_title: AI Engineering Architecture and User Feedback
requests.title: Progressive AI architecture
requests.show: A left-to-right sequence starting with user->model and progressively adding context, guardrails, router/gateway, cache, agent loops, observability, and orchestration
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that each component is introduced to address a specific production need

requests.lesson_title: AI Engineering Architecture and User Feedback
requests.title: Context-enhanced architecture
requests.show: User query flowing into retrieval/tools, retrieved context joining the query, then both entering the model
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that external information is constructed per query rather than memorized inside every prompt

requests.lesson_title: AI Engineering Architecture and User Feedback
requests.title: PII masking workflow
requests.show: Input containing private data -> sensitive-data detector -> placeholder substitution -> external model -> placeholder response -> trusted reverse map -> final restored response
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice which parts must remain inside the trust boundary

requests.lesson_title: AI Engineering Architecture and User Feedback
requests.title: Model gateway
requests.show: Multiple applications connecting to one gateway which fans out to several commercial and self-hosted model endpoints
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that model access and policies are centralized

requests.lesson_title: AI Engineering Architecture and User Feedback
requests.title: Semantic-cache lookup
requests.show: Query -> embedding -> vector search over cached queries -> similarity threshold -> cache hit or normal model pipeline
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that an incorrect similarity decision can return an incorrect answer

requests.lesson_title: AI Engineering Architecture and User Feedback
requests.title: Evaluation-monitoring feedback loop
requests.show: Offline evaluation -> deployment -> monitoring/observability -> production failures -> new evaluation cases -> next release
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that evaluation and production monitoring form one learning loop

requests.lesson_title: AI Engineering Architecture and User Feedback
requests.title: AI request trace
requests.show: A horizontal timeline showing router, retrieval, model, tool, guardrail, and final response spans with latency/cost annotations
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice how one trace connects component-level failures to the user-visible result

requests.lesson_title: AI Engineering Architecture and User Feedback
requests.title: AI product data flywheel
requests.show: Product -> users -> interaction/feedback data -> evaluation/training/personalization -> improved product
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that product usage can become a model-improvement advantage only when feedback is responsibly captured

requests.lesson_title: AI Engineering Architecture and User Feedback
requests.title: Workflow-integrated feedback
requests.show: A generated suggestion with actions accept, edit, regenerate, ignore, and share, each producing different feedback strengths
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that useful feedback can be collected as a natural side effect of accomplishing the task

requests.lesson_title: AI Engineering Architecture and User Feedback
requests.title: Feedback bias map
requests.show: A central 'user feedback' node connected to leniency, randomness, position, length/preference, and recency bias
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that raw feedback needs interpretation before it becomes training or product truth

requests.lesson_title: AI Engineering Architecture and User Feedback
requests.title: Degenerate feedback loop
requests.show: Ranking -> exposure -> user feedback -> model update -> stronger ranking, shown as an amplifying cycle
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that model outputs influence the data that later trains the model

requests.lesson_title: From LLMs to Agents and the Model Context Protocol
requests.title: Evolution from chatbot to augmented LLM
requests.show: A four-stage diagram showing basic LLM chat, RAG with a vector database, function calling with an execution environment, and an augmented LLM with retrieval, tools, and memory
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that each stage adds capability around the model rather than replacing the model itself

requests.lesson_title: From LLMs to Agents and the Model Context Protocol
requests.title: Agent Reason-Act-Observe loop
requests.show: A circular diagram with Reason → Act → Observe → Reason, with environment inputs such as tools, files, prompt, and history feeding the Act stage and tool results feeding Observe
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that the next action depends on observed feedback, which is what makes the process adaptive

requests.lesson_title: From LLMs to Agents and the Model Context Protocol
requests.title: Fixed workflow versus autonomous agent
requests.show: Two side-by-side diagrams: left shows a predetermined code-controlled chain of LLM calls; right shows an LLM choosing among tools inside repeated action-feedback loops
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that both may use LLMs and tools, but control of the path is different

requests.lesson_title: From LLMs to Agents and the Model Context Protocol
requests.title: M×N integration problem transformed into M+N with MCP
requests.show: First panel shows three model applications each connected separately to four tools, producing twelve links; second panel shows the applications connecting through MCP clients to MCP servers so each side needs only its protocol connection
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice how a shared protocol removes repeated pairwise connectors

requests.lesson_title: From LLMs to Agents and the Model Context Protocol
requests.title: MCP host-client-server architecture
requests.show: A diagram showing a host application containing an LLM and MCP client, the client communicating across a transport with an MCP server, and the server exposing tools, resources, and prompts
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that the MCP client belongs to the host side, while capabilities are exposed by the server side

requests.lesson_title: From LLMs to Agents and the Model Context Protocol
requests.title: Local and remote MCP transports
requests.show: A split diagram showing a local host and MCP server connected through stdio on one side, and a host connecting to a remote MCP server through Streamable HTTP on the other; annotate that JSON-RPC messages travel through either transport
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that the protocol message model stays consistent even though the transport changes

requests.lesson_title: Building Agentic Applications with MCP Clients
requests.title: Host application with LLM and MCP clients
requests.show: A diagram showing a user interacting with one host application that contains both an LLM-provider client and an MCP client; the LLM client points to the model API while the MCP client points to an MCP server
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that the two clients solve different communication problems but are coordinated by the same host

requests.lesson_title: Building Agentic Applications with MCP Clients
requests.title: Wrapped MCP client layer hierarchy
requests.show: A layered diagram showing Host Application → application MCPClient wrapper → SDK Client → Transport → MCP Server
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that the wrapper is an application design choice that adds control without replacing the SDK client

requests.lesson_title: Building Agentic Applications with MCP Clients
requests.title: stdio versus Streamable HTTP client connection
requests.show: A side-by-side architecture: left shows Host + MCP Client launching a local MCP Server subprocess via stdio; right shows Host + MCP Client sending requests to a remote MCP Server URL over Streamable HTTP
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that stdio manages a local process while Streamable HTTP targets a remote service

requests.lesson_title: Building Agentic Applications with MCP Clients
requests.title: Tool discovery and invocation sequence
requests.show: A sequence diagram with Host → MCP Client → MCP Server for list_tools, then Host/LLM selecting one tool, MCP Client calling it, and the server returning one or more content blocks
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that discovery happens before execution and that tool results may be multimodal or multi-part

requests.lesson_title: Building Agentic Applications with MCP Clients
requests.title: End-to-end MCP tool-use loop
requests.show: A sequence diagram showing User → Host → LLM; LLM returns tool request; Host → MCP Client → MCP Server; tool result returns to Host; Host sends tool result back to LLM; LLM either asks for another tool or returns final text to User
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that the model never executes the server function directly—the host and MCP client perform the call

requests.lesson_title: Building Agentic Applications with MCP Clients
requests.title: Intelligent MCP resource loading
requests.show: A flow diagram showing user query plus available resource descriptions feeding a selector, selected names mapped to URIs, resources loaded through MCP, then relevant text/image context attached to the user's message

requests.lesson_title: Advanced MCP Clients and Production Best Practices

requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that internal composition can remain granular while the model-facing action stays simple

requests.lesson_title: Building MCP Servers: Tools, Prompts, and Resources

requests.lesson_title: Building MCP Servers: Tools, Prompts, and Resources

requests.show: A sequence diagram showing resources/list, resource selection, resources/read, contextual use by the application, and a modern subscriptions/listen stream receiving a resource/list or resource update notification
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice the separation between metadata discovery, content loading, and later update awareness

requests.lesson_title: Advanced MCP Servers: Utilities and Client Capabilities

requests.show: A two-column diagram with server utilities on one side and client-provided capabilities on the other, both feeding into tools/prompts/resources

requests.lesson_title: Advanced MCP Servers: Utilities and Client Capabilities

requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that one injected object exposes both static server state and per-request state

requests.lesson_title: Advanced MCP Servers: Utilities and Client Capabilities

requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that progress messages improve UX without changing the final result contract

requests.title: MCP resolver dependency flow
requests.show: A flow diagram showing model-provided arguments and Context feeding resolvers, resolvers obtaining elicitation/sampling/roots values, and the SDK injecting those results before the tool body runs
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that resolved parameters are not chosen by the model

requests.lesson_title: Advanced MCP Servers: Utilities and Client Capabilities
requests.title: Elicitation resolver flow
requests.show: A sequence diagram showing tool call → resolver → client UI → user accept/decline/cancel → validated result → tool body
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that user input is injected by the SDK rather than filled by the model

requests.lesson_title: Advanced MCP Servers: Utilities and Client Capabilities
requests.title: Roots coordination versus real sandboxing
requests.show: A diagram showing a client-declared root passed to a local server, plus a separate true sandbox/OS-permission boundary around the server process
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that roots describe intended scope but the sandbox enforces actual scope

requests.lesson_title: Testing, Securing, and Sharing Your MCP Server

requests.lesson_title: Testing, Securing, and Sharing Your MCP Server

requests.show: A stacked diagram with infrastructure isolation at the bottom, access control in the middle, and observability/supply-chain/HITL controls at the top
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that strong security combines prevention, authorization, and detection/response

requests.lesson_title: Testing, Securing, and Sharing Your MCP Server

requests.show: A triangle labeled Private Data, Untrusted Content, and Third-Party Communication, with a warning in the center and examples of controls that remove one edge
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that security can improve by structurally breaking the dangerous combination

requests.lesson_title: Testing, Securing, and Sharing Your MCP Server
requests.title: Remote MCP deployment stack
requests.show: A layered diagram showing cloud/container → Uvicorn → ASGI app → mounted MCP server → /mcp endpoint, with OAuth/gateway in front

requests.lesson_title: Connecting Clients and Servers: MCP Transports

requests.lesson_title: Connecting Clients and Servers: MCP Transports

requests.lesson_title: Deploying Vision-Language Models for Inference at Scale

Compare fixed maximum KV-cache allocations with many unused spaces against

requests.show:
Show task → think/plan → action/tool → observation → completion decision →

requests.title: Chunking strategies comparison
requests.show: One paragraph shown under fixed-size, sentence/paragraph, recursive, document-structure, and semantic chunking with different boundary placements
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice how each strategy preserves a different kind of structure

requests.title: Embedding similarity heatmap
requests.show: A 4×4 heatmap for happy, joyful, pessimistic, and not optimistic sentences, with the highest off-diagonal similarity between semantically related pairs

requests.title: HNSW hierarchy
requests.show: A four-level graph from sparse landmark nodes at the top to dense local vectors at the bottom, with a query path descending toward a nearby vector

requests.title: Metadata-filtered vector search
requests.show: A large set of company-report vectors narrowed first by company and date metadata, then searched semantically
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that exact structured constraints and semantic similarity solve different parts of the retrieval problem

requests.title: End-to-end RAG failure propagation
requests.show: A pipeline from parsing through chunking, embedding, retrieval, reranking, prompting, and generation with example failure labels under each stage
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that a bad final answer may originate several stages before the LLM

requests.title: Enterprise RAG scaling map
requests.show: Diagram showing data volume, query load, data complexity, retrieval quality, guardrails, and UX surrounding a central RAG pipeline
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that scale affects several interacting dimensions, not one component

requests.title: Distributed ingestion pipeline
requests.show: Source documents fan out to parsing, cleaning, chunking, metadata extraction, embedding workers, then converge on vector and metadata stores with retries and observability
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice parallel stages, checkpoints, and failure isolation

requests.title: Conditional document triage
requests.show: Decision tree routing native PDFs, scanned PDFs, HTML, and malformed files through parser, OCR, boilerplate removal, or quarantine paths
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that different document qualities require different preprocessing

requests.title: Hybrid retrieval fusion
requests.show: Parallel semantic vector search and lexical BM25 search produce ranked lists that are fused before reranking
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that semantic meaning and exact-term evidence are complementary

requests.title: RAG trust boundaries
requests.show: System instructions separated from user query and retrieved documents, with sanitization and output checks around the LLM
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that retrieved context is untrusted data and not an instruction source

requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice how provenance and user controls are integrated into the answer experience

requests.title: RAG response-quality failure tree
requests.show: Decision tree from a bad answer through data coverage, retrieval, generation faithfulness, and prompt design
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice the recommended debugging order and that not every bad answer is an LLM problem

requests.title: Fan-out/gather RAG query architecture
requests.show: Diagram showing an orchestrator calling semantic and lexical search in parallel, gathering candidates, reranking, then calling the LLM
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that parallel independent work reduces additive latency

requests.title: Multi-level RAG caching
requests.show: Layered diagram showing full-response, retrieval, and chunk caches around the orchestrator and retrieval services
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that each cache skips a different amount of downstream work

requests.title: RAG defense-in-depth security layers
requests.show: Diagram showing ingestion security, encrypted data stores with RBAC, permission-filtered retrieval, protected LLM generation, and monitored output
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that security constraints must persist across every transformation

requests.title: Observability plane across RAG microservices

requests.show: Show an application connected either to many individually managed RAG components or to one standardized platform API backed by managed components
requests.learner_should_notice: Notice that the main difference is ownership of infrastructure complexity, not the disappearance of the RAG stages

requests.title: RAG evaluation layers

requests.title: Database system hierarchy

requests.title: Multi-database GenAI architecture
requests.show: Diagram showing a GenAI/RAG application connected to PostgreSQL for users/conversations, a vector database for embeddings, a graph database for document relationships, Redis for caching, and a document database for flexible prompt templates
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that database choice is per problem rather than one database replacing every other type

requests.title: Conversation-message relational schema
requests.show: Simple ER diagram showing `conversations` with primary key `id`, and `messages` with primary key `id` plus foreign key `conversation_id`; draw a one-to-many relationship and note cascade delete
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice how relational modeling connects conversation history

requests.title: Code and database migration history
requests.show: Parallel timelines showing Git commits for application code and Alembic revisions for database schema; arrows should show application versions aligning with schema versions across development/staging/production
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that schema evolution is versioned and deployed deliberately

requests.lesson_title: Authentication and Authorization for GenAI Services
requests.title: Authentication versus authorization
requests.show: Two-stage access diagram showing a user first proving identity, then passing a second permission check for a resource/action
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that knowing who the user is does not automatically grant access

requests.lesson_title: Authentication and Authorization for GenAI Services
requests.title: Authentication methods overview
requests.show: Four-column diagram for Basic credentials, token/JWT, OAuth identity provider, and public/private-key authentication, each showing the client and server interaction at a high level
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should recognize that authentication mechanisms prove identity in different ways

requests.lesson_title: Authentication and Authorization for GenAI Services
requests.title: JWT anatomy
requests.show: Diagram showing a JWT split into header, payload, and signature, with example claims such as user ID, role, issuer, and expiration
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that Base64-style encoding makes token parts compact/readable but the signature is what protects integrity

requests.lesson_title: Authentication and Authorization for GenAI Services
requests.title: User-token entity relationship
requests.show: ER diagram showing users → tokens as a one-to-many relationship, with user role/hashed password and token expiry/active state highlighted
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that token records make revocation and session tracking possible

requests.lesson_title: Authentication and Authorization for GenAI Services
requests.title: Password hashing and salting
requests.show: Registration path showing password + random salt → password-hash algorithm → stored salted hash, and login path showing candidate password verified against the stored hash
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that the plain password is never stored and that the salt makes identical passwords produce different hash records

requests.lesson_title: Authentication and Authorization for GenAI Services
requests.title: JWT lifecycle
requests.show: Flow showing login → issue signed short-lived JWT → client sends Bearer token → server verifies signature/claims and active token record → allow request; separate branches for expiry and logout/revocation
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that token issuance is only the start of the lifecycle

requests.lesson_title: Authentication and Authorization for GenAI Services
requests.title: OAuth state/CSRF protection
requests.show: Two OAuth callback paths: legitimate flow where stored state matches returned state and proceeds, and attacker/forged flow where state mismatches and is rejected
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that state binds the callback to the original login attempt

requests.lesson_title: Authentication and Authorization for GenAI Services
requests.title: RBAC for GenAI models
requests.show: Diagram showing authenticated USER and ADMIN roles flowing through an authorization guard; USER can access text generation while ADMIN can access text and image/premium models
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that model access is enforced in application logic

requests.lesson_title: Authentication and Authorization for GenAI Services
requests.title: ReBAC hierarchy
requests.show: Graph showing a user connected as member of a team, team linked to a private folder, and folder containing conversations/threads; permission inheritance flows through relationships
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that access can come from relationships rather than one global role

requests.lesson_title: Authentication and Authorization for GenAI Services
requests.title: ABAC GenAI policy
requests.show: Policy diagram showing attributes such as `user.plan=paid`, `resource.is_public`, and `upload.has_pii` being evaluated to allow or deny premium-model/document actions
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that policies can be dynamic and context-sensitive

requests.lesson_title: Securing AI Services Against Misuse and Abuse
requests.title: GenAI attack surface
requests.show: A defensive architecture diagram showing user inputs, external documents, model, tools/plugins, downstream systems, and stored sensitive data, with risk markers at prompt injection, malicious external content, unsafe output handling, excessive tool permissions, and resource exhaustion
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that GenAI security spans inputs, model behavior, outputs, integrations, and infrastructure

requests.lesson_title: Securing AI Services Against Misuse and Abuse
requests.title: Guardrail threshold trade-off
requests.show: A horizontal score scale from low to high with a movable threshold; mark false-positive region on one side and false-negative risk on the other
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that threshold selection trades user friction against safety/abuse risk

requests.lesson_title: Securing AI Services Against Misuse and Abuse
requests.title: Rate limiting versus throttling
requests.show: Side-by-side diagram where rate limiting rejects requests after a quota is reached, while throttling lets traffic continue but slows processing/transmission
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that rate limiting controls admission while throttling controls pace

requests.lesson_title: Securing AI Services Against Misuse and Abuse
requests.title: Distributed rate limiting with Redis
requests.show: Load balancer distributing requests to three FastAPI instances, all reading/writing the same Redis rate-limit counters
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice why per-process memory cannot enforce one global quota across replicas

requests.title: AI service optimization map
requests.show: Diagram splitting optimization goals into performance (latency, throughput, memory, cost) and quality (reliability, structure, alignment), with techniques connected to each side: batching/caching/quantization and structured output/prompting/fine-tuning
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that each technique addresses a specific bottleneck rather than being a universal improvement

requests.title: Keyword versus semantic cache
requests.show: Side-by-side flow: keyword cache compares exact text keys, semantic cache embeds queries and compares vectors; show two differently worded but equivalent questions missing exact cache yet hitting semantic cache
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that semantic caching uses meaning rather than exact wording

requests.title: Semantic cache in RAG
requests.show: Diagram showing user query → embedding → semantic cache; cache hit returns documents directly, cache miss queries document vector store and stores retrieved documents in cache before prompt augmentation and LLM generation
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that this cache avoids repeated retrieval while preserving fresh generation

requests.title: Model quantization pipeline
requests.show: Flow showing FP32/high-precision model weights → calibration/scaling/quantization → lower-precision INT8/INT4 model → inference, with memory footprint decreasing along the path
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that quantization changes numeric representation rather than deleting model layers

requests.title: Precision ladder
requests.show: Vertical ladder showing FP32 → FP16/BF16 → INT8 → INT4 → lower-bit formats, with memory decreasing downward and potential quantization error/quality risk increasing
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice the memory-versus-precision trade-off

requests.title: Free-form JSON versus schema-driven structured output
requests.show: Side-by-side pipeline where prompt-only JSON can produce malformed text and parser failure, while schema-driven output produces validated fields matching a Pydantic model
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice why structured output improves downstream reliability

requests.title: Role-Context-Task prompt template
requests.show: Three stacked blocks labeled Role, Context, Task feeding into the LLM, followed by a more precise output
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that clear role, relevant context, and explicit task jointly reduce ambiguity

requests.title: Agentic tool-calling loop
requests.show: Diagram showing user → LLM → tool/function request → application validates/executes tool → observation returned to LLM → final answer, with an authorization/validation gate before execution
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that the model proposes actions while application code controls actual tool execution

requests.title: Verification and validation V-model
requests.show: V-shaped diagram with requirements and design descending toward implementation on the left, then unit/integration/E2E verification ascending on the right
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that tests verify implementation while validation begins from having the correct requirements

requests.title: Testing strategies comparison
requests.show: Three simplified diagrams comparing testing pyramid, trophy, and honeycomb distributions across static/unit/integration/E2E and other testing types
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that the chapter favors strong integration coverage for dependency-heavy GenAI services

requests.title: Pytest yield fixture lifecycle
requests.show: Timeline showing setup → yield fixture into test → assertions → teardown, with a database client created and later closed
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that cleanup is part of fixture ownership rather than being scattered across tests

requests.title: RAG precision and recall sets
requests.show: Venn-style diagram showing expected relevant documents and retrieved documents with overlap as true positives; annotate recall as overlap/expected and precision as overlap/retrieved
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that recall measures completeness while precision measures signal-to-noise

requests.title: Auto-evaluation testing loop
requests.show: Diagram showing test prompt → model under test → candidate response → evaluator model → structured score → assertion threshold
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that evaluator-based tests add a second probabilistic model to the testing system

requests.title: Vertical versus horizontal E2E
requests.show: Side-by-side RAG diagrams: vertical test moving through layers for one upload/storage feature, horizontal test following an entire user scenario from upload through question answering
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that vertical tests are feature-focused while horizontal tests follow broader user journeys

requests.title: Deployment options for a GenAI service
requests.show: Four branches from one FastAPI/GenAI application to VM, serverless function, managed application platform, and container deployment
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that deployment choice depends on workload and operational requirements rather than one universal method

requests.title: VM architecture
requests.show: Physical host hardware → hypervisor → multiple VMs, each with its own guest OS and application
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that each VM carries a full guest operating system and receives virtualized hardware resources

requests.title: Docker layered filesystem
requests.show: Stack showing base OS/Python layer, dependency layer, application-code layer, and a top writable container layer; several containers share immutable image layers
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that image layers are reusable while each running container gets its own ephemeral writable layer

requests.title: Container networking mental model
requests.show: Host containing FastAPI, PostgreSQL, Redis, and Qdrant containers connected through an internal Docker network; only FastAPI has a host-published port
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that internal service-to-service communication does not require publishing every database port

requests.title: Docker Compose GenAI stack
requests.show: Compose-defined server and database containers connected to `genai-net`; DB uses a persistent volume, server exposes port 8000, and secrets/environment values enter the server
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that Compose describes the whole local stack declaratively

requests.title: Docker image optimization funnel
requests.show: Large unoptimized image entering a funnel of minimal base image, externalized artifacts, cache/layer optimization, `.dockerignore`, and multi-stage build, producing a much smaller final production image
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that several independent techniques compound to reduce size and build time

requests.title: Multi-stage Docker build
requests.show: Three stages labeled Base/Builder, Production, and Development; arrows show only selected artifacts copied from earlier stages into a small production image while dev tools remain in the development stage
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that build-time tooling does not need to ship in the final production image

requests.lesson_title: DevOps & Cloud Foundations: From Culture to Your First Workstation
requests.title: Breaking the wall of confusion
requests.show: A before-and-after diagram. On the left, Development and Operations are separated by a wall and exchange a large risky release. On the right, Dev, Ops, QA, Security, and Product collaborate around one continuous delivery flow with shared feedback arrows
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that DevOps changes the organizational flow and ownership model, not merely the toolset

requests.lesson_title: DevOps & Cloud Foundations: From Culture to Your First Workstation
requests.title: DevOps infinity loop
requests.show: An infinity-loop diagram containing the eight stages Plan, Code, Build, Test, Release, Deploy, Operate, and Monitor, with arrows showing continuous movement and monitoring feedback returning toward planning
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that the lifecycle is cyclic and overlapping rather than a one-way project sequence

requests.lesson_title: DevOps & Cloud Foundations: From Culture to Your First Workstation
requests.title: CI versus Continuous Delivery versus Continuous Deployment
requests.show: Three horizontal pipelines. CI stops after a tested build artifact; Continuous Delivery continues through staging but shows a manual approval gate before production; Continuous Deployment continues automatically into production
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that the main distinction between Delivery and Deployment is the final production approval gate

requests.lesson_title: DevOps & Cloud Foundations: From Culture to Your First Workstation
requests.title: Cloud service model responsibility stack
requests.show: A layered stack comparing on-premises, IaaS, PaaS, and SaaS across networking, storage, servers, virtualization, operating system, runtime, application, and data, clearly showing which layers are managed by the customer versus the provider
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that moving from IaaS to PaaS to SaaS trades direct control for less operational responsibility

requests.lesson_title: DevOps & Cloud Foundations: From Culture to Your First Workstation
requests.title: VS Code DevOps workspace anatomy
requests.show: A screenshot-style diagram of VS Code with the Explorer, Search, Source Control, Run/Debug, Extensions icons, editor pane, and integrated terminal labeled
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that source files, Git workflow, extensions, and terminal commands can be managed from one workspace

requests.lesson_title: Mastering Version Control with Git and GitHub
requests.title: GitHub new-repository screen
requests.show: A GitHub repository-creation page showing repository name, description, visibility choice, README initialization option, and create button
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice the minimum settings needed to initialize a repository before cloning it

requests.lesson_title: Mastering Version Control with Git and GitHub
requests.title: Git merge-conflict markers
requests.show: A code-editor view showing `<<<<<<< HEAD`, `=======`, and `>>>>>>> main`, with annotations identifying current change, incoming change, and the final manually resolved line
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that Git presents both competing versions and requires a human to decide the intended final content

requests.show: A three-stage flow: Dockerfile instructions → `docker build` → Docker image → `docker run` → running container, with one image branching to multiple containers

requests.show: A network flow diagram showing Browser → localhost:4000 on host → Docker mapping → port 8080 inside container → Gunicorn/Flask
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that host port 4000 and container port 8080 are different endpoints connected by `-p 4000:8080`

requests.title: Build-run-push Docker workflow
requests.show: A left-to-right diagram showing source + Dockerfile → docker build → local image → docker run → local container, with another arrow from local image → docker tag/docker push → Docker Hub registry → docker pull/run on another machine
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that the same versioned image artifact can move from local development to a registry and then to another environment

requests.lesson_title: Introduction to Infrastructure as Code with Terraform
requests.title: Click-ops versus Infrastructure as Code
requests.show: A side-by-side diagram. Left side shows a human manually clicking through cloud-console screens to create resources. Right side shows version-controlled Terraform files flowing through Terraform into cloud APIs to create the same resources
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that IaC turns manual infrastructure steps into repeatable, reviewable configuration

requests.lesson_title: Introduction to Infrastructure as Code with Terraform
requests.title: Terraform code-state-cloud relationship
requests.show: A three-part diagram showing HCL configuration on the left, `terraform.tfstate` in the middle as the mapping layer, and real AWS resources on the right
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that state connects Terraform resource addresses in code to real infrastructure objects

requests.lesson_title: Introduction to Infrastructure as Code with Terraform
requests.title: Terraform variables and outputs
requests.show: A diagram showing `terraform.tfvars` and input variables feeding into `main.tf`, Terraform creating an S3 bucket, then an output block exposing the bucket ARN
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that variables parameterize configuration while outputs expose useful resource attributes

requests.title: Continuous Integration feedback loop
requests.show: A loop showing developer commit → push/pull request → CI runner → build → automated tests → pass/fail feedback returning immediately to the developer
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that CI's main value is fast feedback after small integrations

requests.title: GitHub Actions hierarchy
requests.show: A hierarchy diagram showing Event → Workflow → Jobs → Runner per job → ordered Steps, with some steps using reusable Actions and others executing shell commands
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice the difference between a workflow, job, step, action, and runner

requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice how the Docker image URI becomes the bridge between the build job and Terraform deployment

requests.title: From Docker container to Kubernetes orchestration
requests.show: A progression diagram showing one Docker container on a laptop, then many containers across multiple servers, followed by Kubernetes managing placement, health, networking, scaling, and updates
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that orchestration solves lifecycle and scale problems that appear after containerization

requests.title: Kubernetes cluster architecture
requests.show: A diagram with the control plane at the top connected through the Kubernetes API to three worker Nodes below, each running Pods
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that the control plane manages desired state while Nodes run workloads

requests.title: Kubernetes reconciliation loop
requests.show: A circular diagram showing desired state = 3 Pods, actual state = 2 Pods, controller detects difference, creates replacement Pod, actual state returns to 3
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that self-healing comes from continuous desired-vs-actual reconciliation

requests.title: Kubernetes Service traffic routing
requests.show: A diagram showing Browser → NodePort → Service with stable DNS/IP → two Flask Pods labeled app=flask-app, with arrows from the Service load-balancing across both Pods
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that the Service is stable while Pods can be replaced

requests.title: Helm chart templating model
requests.show: A diagram showing Helm Chart templates + values.yaml → Helm render/install → generated Deployment, Service, ConfigMap, and other Kubernetes resources → Kubernetes cluster
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that the same templates can be reused with different environment-specific values

requests.title: Monitoring versus observability
requests.show: A side-by-side diagram. Monitoring side shows predefined dashboards watching CPU, memory, latency, and errors. Observability side shows an engineer starting with an unexpected symptom and exploring correlated logs, metrics, and traces to discover a root cause
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that monitoring answers predefined questions while observability supports exploratory investigation

requests.title: Distributed trace waterfall
requests.show: A trace waterfall for one request showing Frontend, Auth Service, User Service, and Database spans with horizontal duration bars, where the Database span is dramatically longer than the others
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that traces reveal where one request spends its time across services

requests.title: ELK centralized logging pipeline
requests.show: A diagram showing multiple application containers sending logs into Logstash, Logstash transforming and forwarding them to Elasticsearch, and Kibana querying Elasticsearch for search and dashboards
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that logs from many services converge into one searchable system

requests.title: End-to-end observability incident workflow
requests.show: A flow showing Alert → Grafana metric spike → distributed trace bottleneck → Kibana log error → identified root cause → remediation → follow-up improvement

requests.show: A diagram showing a configured GCP VM disk being preserved, converted into a custom image, then reused to create multiple identical VM instances

requests.lesson_title: Serverless Deployment with Google Cloud Run

requests.lesson_title: Serverless Deployment with Google Cloud Run
requests.title: Cloud Run build-and-deploy flow
requests.show: A diagram showing local/uploaded source → Cloud Build → container registry → Cloud Run service → managed instances → service URL and metrics

requests.lesson_title: Serverless Deployment with Google Cloud Run

requests.lesson_title: Serverless Deployment with Google Cloud Run

requests.show: A diagram showing HTTPS frontend on port 443 → host rules → Flask backend service → flask-neg → flask-app and Streamlit backend service → streamlit-neg → streamlit-app

requests.lesson_title: Serverless Deployment with Google Cloud Run

requests.lesson_title: Serverless Deployment with AWS ECS Fargate

requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that ECR is the handoff point between local build and Fargate runtime

requests.lesson_title: Serverless Deployment with AWS ECS Fargate
requests.title: ALB and ECS security-group boundary
requests.show: A diagram showing internet/trusted client → alb-sg → ALB → ecs-sg-tasks → Flask:5000 and Streamlit:8501 Fargate tasks, with direct internet-to-task traffic blocked

requests.lesson_title: Serverless Deployment with AWS ECS Fargate
requests.title: ALB host-based routing
requests.show: A diagram showing one ALB listener with three rules: flask hostname → flask-tg, streamlit hostname → streamlit-tg, default/unmatched → fixed 403
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that the ALB replaces the earlier Nginx host-routing layer

requests.lesson_title: Serverless Deployment with AWS ECS Fargate

requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that operational debugging no longer depends on SSH access to a host

requests.lesson_title: Serverless Deployment with AWS ECS Fargate
requests.title: HTTPS ALB termination
requests.show: A diagram showing browser HTTPS → ALB port 443 with ACM certificate → host rule → Flask or Streamlit target group → Fargate task over internal application port
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that TLS terminates at the ALB rather than inside the application container

requests.lesson_title: Serverless Deployment with AWS ECS Fargate
requests.title: Fargate task autoscaling
requests.show: A diagram showing one ECS service with task definition size fixed, task count increasing from 1 to multiple replicas as average CPU crosses a target, then shrinking within min/max bounds
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice the difference between per-task resources and number of tasks

requests.title: Reactive LLM versus goal-directed agent
requests.show: A side-by-side diagram. Left: User -> LLM -> Text response -> Stop. Right: User goal -> Agent -> Plan -> Tool actions -> Observe results -> Continue/finish
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that the agent has a continuing control loop instead of a single prompt-response interaction

requests.lesson_title: Core Components: LLMs, Prompting, and Agents

requests.show: A two-part diagram. Left: training text -> tokenization -> prediction -> loss -> backpropagation -> updated weights. Right: prompt -> tokenization -> model -> next-token probabilities -> sampling -> generated token -> repeated generation

requests.lesson_title: Core Components: LLMs, Prompting, and Agents
requests.title: Plain text versus JSON tokenization
requests.show: Show the same semantic information written once as simple prose and once as JSON, with token boundaries highlighted so the JSON representation visibly contains more token pieces
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that formatting characters and field names also consume tokens

requests.lesson_title: Core Components: LLMs, Prompting, and Agents
requests.title: Sequential tool chain versus parallel tool calls
requests.show: Left: Tool A -> result -> Tool B -> result. Right: one agent step fans out to Tool A, Tool B, and Tool C simultaneously, then merges results
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that dependency determines whether calls must be sequential or can safely run in parallel

requests.lesson_title: Actions with Model Context Protocol for AI Agents
requests.title: Before MCP versus with MCP
requests.show: Left: one agent connected to filesystem, database, web API, and SaaS service through four different custom connectors. Right: the agent connects through MCP to reusable servers that wrap those services
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that MCP standardizes the integration boundary rather than eliminating the underlying services

requests.lesson_title: Actions with Model Context Protocol for AI Agents
requests.title: STDIO versus remote SSE connection
requests.show: Left: Agent launches MCP server subprocess and communicates through stdin/stdout. Right: Agent connects over HTTP to a separately running MCP server
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice the difference in process ownership, networking, and sharing

requests.lesson_title: Actions with Model Context Protocol for AI Agents
requests.title: MCP Inspector workflow
requests.show: A small debugging flow: MCP server -> Inspector -> list tools -> inspect schema -> run tool manually -> inspect raw response, followed by Agent integration only after success
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that server behavior should be verified independently before blaming the agent

requests.show: Left: one overloaded agent with many tools and responsibilities. Right: several specialized agents connected through a clear flow, each with a small tool set
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that decomposition reduces responsibility per agent but adds coordination boundaries

requests.show: A diagram with four labeled blocks: Decision-making, Control, Communication, Coordination. Under each, show one guiding question: Who decides? Who acts? What context moves? How does execution proceed?
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should use these four questions as an architecture checklist

requests.title: Agent flow graph and trace relationship
requests.show: Show a static graph Research -> Planning -> Filesystem beside a runtime timeline showing actual calls, tool use, latency, and a handoff event
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that a graph documents possible structure while a trace shows what actually happened

requests.title: Decomposition versus planning
requests.show: Left: one large goal breaking into several subproblems. Right: the same subproblems connected by arrows showing order, dependencies, and parallel branches
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that decomposition defines the pieces while planning defines how the pieces fit together

requests.title: Agent with Sequential Thinking scratchpad
requests.show: Show Agent/LLM connected to a Sequential Thinking MCP server. The scratchpad contains Thought 1, Thought 2, revision of Thought 1, branch B, and status metadata. Also show ordinary action tools beside it
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that the MCP server stores structured reasoning state while the agent still makes decisions

requests.lesson_title: Working with Memory and Knowledge RAG for Agents
requests.title: External storage versus bounded context
requests.show: Show a large database/vector store containing many documents and memories on the left, a retrieval filter in the middle, and a small context window feeding an LLM on the right
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that retrieval selects a small relevant subset from a much larger store

requests.lesson_title: Working with Memory and Knowledge RAG for Agents
requests.title: RAG ingestion and retrieval phases

requests.lesson_title: Working with Memory and Knowledge RAG for Agents
requests.title: Cosine similarity intuition
requests.show: Draw two vector pairs from the same origin: one pair with a small angle labeled high similarity, and another with a large angle labeled low similarity
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that cosine comparison focuses on direction rather than vector length

requests.lesson_title: Working with Memory and Knowledge RAG for Agents
requests.title: Semantic embedding clusters in 3D
requests.show: A 3D scatter plot with visually grouped clusters such as sky/blue sentences, dog/fox sentences, and breakfast/food sentences
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that semantically related texts cluster near one another after dimensionality reduction

requests.lesson_title: Working with Memory and Knowledge RAG for Agents
requests.title: Hybrid retrieval with Reciprocal Rank Fusion
requests.show: Show keyword search producing ranked list A and vector search producing ranked list B, then an RRF fusion block merging them into one final ranked list
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that fusion combines rank positions from different scoring systems

requests.lesson_title: Building Robust Agents with Evaluation and Feedback
requests.title: Independent evaluation versus colluding evaluation
requests.show: Left: generator and evaluator share the same blind spot and both approve a wrong answer. Right: generator is checked by a differently configured evaluator plus periodic human review
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that multiple agents do not automatically equal independent evidence

requests.lesson_title: Building Robust Agents with Evaluation and Feedback
requests.title: Rubric evaluation matrix
requests.show: A table-like visual with rows Accuracy, Grounding, Tool Use, Completeness, Error Handling and columns scores 1 through 5, with short descriptions for weak versus strong performance
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that rubrics make multiple quality dimensions explicit

requests.lesson_title: Building Robust Agents with Evaluation and Feedback
requests.title: From trace annotation to regression dataset
requests.show: Show Trace -> Reviewer annotation -> Stored labeled span -> Dataset -> New agent version -> Regression experiment
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice how one manual observation becomes reusable evaluation data

requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that agent placement changes the trust boundary and communication path

requests.show: Show Browser Realtime Agent requesting an ephemeral credential from Backend Auth, then connecting to the realtime model. The permanent provider key remains only on the backend
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that the browser never receives the long-lived server credential

requests.title: Agent container anatomy
requests.show: Show Host Machine -> Docker Container containing Python runtime, application code, dependencies, and Agent API, with port mapping to the host and secrets injected at runtime rather than baked into the image
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice what belongs inside the image versus what should be supplied at runtime

requests.title: Docker Compose multi-agent stack
requests.show: Show Web/Realtime service connected to Image Agent and Web Search Agent containers, with each service in its own container and all managed by one Compose file
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that Compose coordinates deployment without merging the services into one process

requests.title: End-to-end agent observability
requests.show: Show UI -> Gateway -> Agent -> Tool -> Model with trace spans across the whole path. Beside it list Operational, Quality, and Product metrics plus structured logs with PII redaction
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that observability covers both technical operation and whether the agent actually delivers value

requests.lesson_title: Exploring the Cognitive Agent That Thinks, Monitors, and Adapts
requests.title: Three theoretical foundations mapped to architecture
requests.show: Three columns: Minsky -> specialized modules; Baars -> shared cognitive workspace; Kahneman -> fast/deep routing through attention
requests.learner_should_notice: Learner should notice that each theory contributes one concrete design principle

requests.lesson_title: Exploring the Cognitive Agent That Thinks, Monitors, and Adapts
